title: Add to Cart really puts the product in the cart
group_en: Add to Cart and cart that work
group_ar: الـ Add to Cart والـ cart شغالين صح
pass: After our Add to Cart click on the product page, on phone and desktop, the cart icon count changes and the cart page lists that product with its price.
fails: The click gives no feedback, the cart count stays the same, or the cart page is empty after the click, while an add_to_cart / AddToCart event may still fire.
validate: Browser: on the product page click Add to Cart once (phone and desktop), read the cart icon count, open the cart and check that the cart DOM lists the product; screenshot both. Record any add_to_cart / AddToCart hits in network and dataLayer. Quote GA4 view_item→add_to_cart (GA4-02) beside it as context.
action: Forward the screenshots to the developer: the Add to Cart button must put the item in the cart and show it, phone first.
done_when: Our re-scan adds the product on phone and desktop, the cart lists it and the cart count changes.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks that can't add can't buy, so CVR and ROAS are likely lower than the ads deserve; if the event still fires, the platforms learn from adds that never happened.
selected_because: The core post-click break the buyer can't see in Ads Manager, proven by our own add-to-cart visit.

title: Shipping cost shown before checkout
pass: The product page or the cart states the shipping cost, or the free-shipping rule, before the checkout button.
fails: No shipping cost on the product page or in the cart; the shopper first sees it inside checkout.
validate: Browser (phone): read product page and cart DOM after our add for shipping cost text or a shipping estimator; screenshot. GA4: quote add_to_cart→begin_checkout and begin_checkout→purchase (GA4-03, GA4-04); mark the point high when either step is below the tool's benchmark. Checkout itself: not checked.
action: Ask the store owner to show the shipping cost (or the free-shipping rule) on the product page and in the cart.
done_when: Shipping cost text is visible on the product page and in the cart on phone in our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Shoppers from ads who meet a surprise cost in checkout leave after you paid for the click; showing it earlier likely lifts CVR and lowers CPA on the same spend.
selected_because: High-impact, tested leak (3 of 5 stores failed) tied to the cart and checkout funnel steps.

title: Local payment options visible before checkout
pass: The product page or cart shows the payment methods GCC shoppers look for (such as mada, Apple Pay, Tabby or Tamara, cash on delivery) as icons, widgets or text.
fails: No payment information until checkout; cash on delivery or buy-now-pay-later never mentioned.
validate: Browser: read product page and cart DOM, image alt text and network for payment icons and BNPL widget scripts (Tabby, Tamara); screenshot. GA4: quote begin_checkout→purchase (GA4-04); raise to high when that step is below the tool's benchmark. Methods offered inside checkout: not checked.
action: Ask the owner to show accepted payment methods near Add to Cart and in the cart; the developer adds the BNPL widget if the store uses Tabby or Tamara.
done_when: Payment icons or a BNPL widget are visible on the product page and cart in our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Paid shoppers who can't see their way to pay drop before checkout, so CVR likely reads lower and CPA higher than the traffic deserves.
selected_because: High-impact GCC conversion lever, visible on the storefront and tied to the checkout step in GA4.

title: Each paid campaign lands on a page that fits it
pass: Top paid campaigns land on the product or collection they promote, and any offer named in the campaign shows on the landing page's first screen.
fails: Paid sessions land on the home page, or the landing page doesn't show the product or offer the campaign points to.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days, dimensions sessionCampaignName + landingPage for paid channels, metrics sessions, addToCarts, ecommercePurchases; flag campaigns whose main landing page is the home page and compare their add-to-cart rate with the store's. Browser: visit the top campaign landing URL (focus.campaignLandingUrl), screenshot the first screen, read title, H1 and offer text. The ad itself is not visible: mark copy match 'check against the ad in Ads Manager'.
action: Point each campaign at the product or collection it sells; ask the owner for a landing page that repeats the ad's offer where none exists.
done_when: Each top paid campaign's main landing page in GA4 is the product or collection it promotes, and the offer text is on its first screen.
why_it_matters: A click that lands on a page that doesn't match the ad has to search again, so CVR is likely lower and CPA higher; a matching page also helps Google's landing page experience.
selected_because: The highest-impact message-match point in the pool, measurable from GA4 campaign and landing-page data plus our visit.

title: Cart shows the full total before checkout
pass: The cart shows a clear total with every extra cost known at that point stated (VAT included or listed, cash-on-delivery fee, other fees).
fails: The cart shows only the item subtotal; VAT or a cash-on-delivery fee appears only later.
validate: Browser: after our add, read the cart DOM for subtotal, fee lines, VAT wording and a total line; screenshot. GA4: quote add_to_cart→begin_checkout (GA4-03) beside it.
action: Ask the owner to show the total and any fees (cash-on-delivery fee, VAT) in the cart, not only in checkout.
done_when: The cart in our re-scan shows a total line and states VAT and any fee.
why_it_matters: Fees that appear late push paid shoppers out of checkout, so fixing it likely raises CVR on clicks you already paid for.
selected_because: High-impact hidden-cost leak, checked on the cart page we can reach.

title: Paid landing pages that show 'page not found'
pass: None of the landing pages that get paid sessions return an error or a 'not found' page, and the 404 page offers search or a way back.
fails: Ads or old links send paid sessions to deleted products or a dead page with no way back.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days, dimensions landingPagePlusQueryString + pageTitle + sessionDefaultChannelGroup (paid channels), metric sessions; flag titles that read as not-found pages. Crawl: request the top paid landing URLs and record HTTP status; check menu and footer links and what the 404 page offers.
action: Change the ad URLs that point to dead pages; ask the developer to redirect deleted product URLs to the closest live product or collection.
done_when: No paid landing page in GA4 over the last 14 days shows a not-found title, and the listed URLs return a live page.
why_it_matters: Every paid click to a dead page is spend with no chance to convert, so CAC is higher than it needs to be right now.
selected_because: A measured waste of paid clicks the buyer can fix in the ads the same day.

title: Advertised products that can't be bought
pass: The most-viewed products are in stock, every variant can be selected, and Add to Cart is active.
fails: A top-viewed product is sold out or its variants can't be chosen, while traffic keeps landing on it.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days, dimension itemName, metrics itemsViewed and itemsAddedToCart; list the top-viewed items with zero adds or the lowest add rate (new computation). Browser: open the top product (focus.productUrl) and read stock text, variant state and whether Add to Cart is enabled.
action: Pause or switch ads that send traffic to sold-out products; ask the owner to restock or hide them.
done_when: No top-viewed product in GA4 has zero adds over 14 days, and our visit finds Add to Cart enabled on the top product.
why_it_matters: Clicks on products nobody can buy are paid traffic that can't convert, so CAC is higher than it needs to be right now.
selected_because: Wasted paid clicks shown from the store's own product data, with a fix in the buyer's hands.

title: Campaign tags survive to the landing page
pass: A landing URL with UTMs and a click ID reaches the final page in one hop with the tags intact, and internal links carry no UTMs.
fails: Redirects (http, www, language or app redirects) drop UTMs or click IDs, or internal links carry UTMs that reset the source.
validate: Browser: open the home page and top product with test UTMs and fbclid / gclid / ttclid added, record every redirect hop and the final URL; crawl internal links for utm_ parameters.
action: Send the redirect list to the developer: keep the query string on every redirect and remove UTMs from internal links.
done_when: Our tagged test URLs land in one hop with UTMs and click IDs intact, and no internal link has UTMs.
why_it_matters: When tags drop on the way in, paid sales show as direct or organic, so reported ROAS likely reads lower than real and winning campaigns can get cut.
selected_because: Answers 'is the number real?' at the landing step; measured by our own tagged visit.

title: Cart price matches the product page price
group_en: Product page that converts paid traffic
group_ar: صفحة المنتج اللي بتحوّل الـ paid traffic
pass: The product page shows the price with currency near Add to Cart; a sale price shows the old price; the cart shows the same price after our add.
fails: Price missing or without currency, the discount unclear, or the cart price differs from the product page.
validate: Browser: read the price, currency and any compare-at price on the product page, then the line price in the cart after our add; flag any difference; screenshot both.
action: Ask the owner or developer to make the product page and cart show the same price, with currency and the old price on sale items.
done_when: Our re-scan finds the same price on the product page and in the cart, with currency shown.
why_it_matters: A price that changes between the ad, the page and the cart breaks trust after the click, so CVR likely drops on the same paid traffic.
selected_because: A concrete, checkable price mismatch on the buy path, beyond a generic 'price clarity' item.

title: Phone layout works for mobile paid traffic
group_en: Product page that converts paid traffic
group_ar: صفحة المنتج اللي بتحوّل الـ paid traffic
pass: On a phone, the home, product and cart pages have no sideways scroll, readable text and buttons large enough to tap.
fails: Sideways scroll, cut-off buttons, tiny tap targets or small text on the phone product page or cart.
validate: Browser (phone): compare document width with the viewport, measure tap-target and font sizes on home, product and cart; screenshot. GA4: quote mobile vs desktop conversion (GA4-05) beside it.
action: Send the screenshots to the developer to fix the overflow and enlarge the buttons on phone.
done_when: Our phone re-scan finds no sideways scroll and no undersized buttons on product and cart.
why_it_matters: Most paid social clicks come from phones; a broken phone page likely holds mobile CVR down and CPA up.
selected_because: Ties a visible phone layout fault to the GA4 mobile vs desktop gap.

title: Landing page shows fast on phones
pass: No autoplay hero video on the phone first screen, text files compressed, static files cached, and text visible while Arabic fonts load.
fails: A heavy autoplay video, uncompressed files, short cache, or text invisible until the font loads.
validate: Browser (phone): record first-screen media, response encoding and cache headers, font-display, and time to first visible text. Ad-side link click to landing page view data is not available: mark 'compare link clicks with LPV in Ads Manager'.
action: Ask the developer to replace the phone hero video with an image, turn on compression and caching, and show text while fonts load.
done_when: Our phone re-scan finds no autoplay hero video, compressed text, long cache on static files and text visible during font load.
why_it_matters: People who leave before the page shows never count as a landing page view, so you pay for clicks that never saw the store.
selected_because: The click-to-landing-page-view gap, measured with headless timing only.

title: Clear checkout button in the cart
group_en: Add to Cart and cart that work
group_ar: الـ Add to Cart والـ cart شغالين صح
pass: After our add, the phone cart shows one clear checkout button in the first screen, not hidden by popups or upsells.
fails: The checkout button is missing, below the fold on phone, or covered by a popup or upsell block.
validate: Browser (phone): after our add, find the checkout button in the cart DOM, record its position against the viewport and any overlay; screenshot. GA4: quote add_to_cart→begin_checkout (GA4-03).
action: Ask the developer to place one visible checkout button at the top of the phone cart and remove anything covering it.
done_when: Our phone re-scan shows the checkout button in the cart's first screen with nothing on top of it.
why_it_matters: Shoppers who added from an ad but can't find the next step stall in the cart, so CVR likely reads lower than the traffic deserves.
selected_because: Directly tied to the cart-to-checkout step and checked on our own cart.

title: Cart doesn't force sign-in before checkout
group_en: Add to Cart and cart that work
group_ar: الـ Add to Cart والـ cart شغالين صح
pass: The cart's checkout path offers guest checkout or a phone-number step, with no 'log in to checkout' wall shown on the cart.
fails: The cart shows only 'log in' or 'create account' before checkout.
validate: Browser: read the cart DOM after our add for login-only buttons, account prompts or a guest option; screenshot. Steps after the cart: not checked.
action: Ask the owner to turn on guest checkout or phone-number checkout in the store settings.
done_when: Our re-scan finds no login-only wall on the cart.
why_it_matters: New shoppers from cold ads rarely have an account; a forced login likely cuts CVR on the traffic you pay most to win.
selected_because: A known checkout blocker that can be seen on the cart page without going further.

title: Landing page speaks the shopper's language
pass: Pages declare the right lang and dir, an Arabic version exists with a visible switcher, and Arabic-language paid sessions land on Arabic pages.
fails: Arabic-language sessions land on English pages, or Arabic pages render with broken right-to-left layout.
validate: Browser/crawl: read html lang, dir, hreflang and the language switcher on landing and product pages; screenshot the Arabic product page. GA4: run_report 28 days, dimensions language + landingPage for paid channels; flag Arabic-language sessions landing on English pages (new computation).
action: Point Arabic ads at the Arabic URLs; ask the developer to fix lang, dir and right-to-left layout.
done_when: GA4 shows Arabic-language paid sessions landing on Arabic pages, and our visit finds correct lang and dir.
why_it_matters: An Arabic ad that lands on an English or broken page loses the shopper the ad just won, so CVR likely drops and CPA rises.
selected_because: Message match by language, measurable from GA4 language data and the page markup.

title: Free-shipping threshold set against order value
pass: If the store has free shipping above an amount, the amount shows on the product page and in the cart, and it sits a reachable step above the store's GA4 AOV.
fails: No threshold shown, or the threshold is far from the store's typical order, so it doesn't move order value.
validate: Browser: read free-shipping text on the product page and cart, including any 'add X more' message after our add. GA4: quote AOV from the computed facts and compare it with the threshold found (new computation).
action: Ask the owner to show the free-shipping amount in the cart and set it just above the current AOV.
done_when: The cart shows the threshold with a progress message, and GA4 AOV is tracked over 28 days after the change.
why_it_matters: A threshold set near the typical order raises AOV, so ROAS likely rises at the same CAC.
selected_because: An AOV lever tied to the store's own GA4 AOV, not a free-shipping bar taken alone.

title: Ways to add a second item
pass: The product page or cart offers related items, bundles or multi-buy offers, and GA4 items per order is above one item.
fails: No cross-sell or bundle anywhere, and GA4 shows orders are almost all single items.
validate: Browser: detect recommendation blocks, bundle or multi-buy offers on the product page and cart (DOM and known app scripts). GA4: compute items per order = itemsPurchased ÷ transactions, 28 days (new computation).
action: Ask the owner to add related products or a bundle on the best-selling product page and in the cart.
done_when: A cross-sell or bundle block is visible on product page or cart, and GA4 items per order is tracked over 28 days after.
why_it_matters: More items per order raises AOV, so ROAS likely rises at the same CAC.
selected_because: AOV lever made measurable with the store's own items-per-order figure.

title: Delivery time shown before checkout
pass: The product page or listing states the expected delivery time.
fails: No delivery time anywhere before checkout.
validate: Browser: read product page, collection and cart DOM for delivery-time text; screenshot. GA4: quote add_to_cart→begin_checkout (GA4-03) beside it.
action: Ask the owner to add the delivery time to the product page, near Add to Cart.
done_when: Delivery time text is visible on the product page in our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Shoppers from ads who don't know when it arrives hesitate in the cart, so stating it likely lifts CVR.
selected_because: Tested and failed in 3 of 5 stores; clear page fact tied to the cart step.

title: Promo codes from your ads have a place to go
group_en: Add to Cart and cart that work
group_ar: الـ Add to Cart والـ cart شغالين صح
pass: The cart shows a discount code field, or the store applies codes from the link automatically.
fails: Ads or influencers give a code, but the cart has no field, so shoppers hunt for it or leave.
validate: Browser: read the cart DOM after our add for a discount code input. Whether a given code works: not checked.
action: Ask the owner to show the discount field in the cart, or use auto-apply discount links in the ads.
done_when: Our re-scan finds a discount field in the cart, or the ad links apply the code.
why_it_matters: Code-based campaigns lose shoppers who can't use the code, so CVR on those campaigns likely reads lower.
selected_because: Directly affects code-based paid and influencer campaigns; visible on the cart.

title: Product page answers the buying questions
group_en: Product page that converts paid traffic
group_ar: صفحة المنتج اللي بتحوّل الـ paid traffic
pass: The top product page has a description in the shopper's language with size, material or specs, and key benefits near Add to Cart.
fails: A one-line or empty description, missing size or specs, or text only in another language.
validate: Browser: on the top product (focus.productUrl) read description length and language, and look for size, material or spec fields; screenshot. GA4: flag high only when view_item→add_to_cart (GA4-02) for that product is below the store's average.
action: Ask the content owner to add size, material and key benefits to the top advertised product first.
done_when: The top product page shows a full description with specs in our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Paid visitors who can't find the facts don't add to cart, so CVR on product ads likely stays low.
selected_because: Merged product-information items, tied to the product's own add-to-cart rate.

title: Enough product photos on the top product
group_en: Product page that converts paid traffic
group_ar: صفحة المنتج اللي بتحوّل الـ paid traffic
pass: The top advertised product shows several photos, including the product in use.
fails: One photo only, or low-quality images on the product page.
validate: Browser: count gallery images on the top product (focus.productUrl) and record their sizes; screenshot. GA4: flag high only when that product's view_item→add_to_cart is below the store's average.
action: Ask the content owner to add more photos, including in-use shots, to the top advertised product.
done_when: The top product page shows more than one photo in our re-scan.
why_it_matters: The ad's image sets the expectation; a thin gallery on the landing product likely holds add-to-cart rate and CVR down.
selected_because: Catalogue lever on the product the ads send traffic to, tied to its GA4 add rate.

title: WhatsApp or contact visible on the product page
group_en: Trust at the moment of buying
pass: The product page shows a working WhatsApp or contact link without leaving the page.
fails: No contact route on the product page, or a broken WhatsApp link.
validate: Browser: read product page DOM for wa.me / WhatsApp links, phone or chat widget, and check the link format; screenshot.
action: Ask the owner to add a WhatsApp button on product pages.
done_when: Our re-scan finds a working WhatsApp or contact link on the product page.
why_it_matters: Cold paid shoppers with one question leave if they can't ask, so a visible contact route likely lifts CVR.
selected_because: A GCC trust lever on the page paid traffic lands on.

title: Return policy reachable from the product page
group_en: Trust at the moment of buying
pass: The product page or cart links to a return policy or states the return terms.
fails: Return terms only in the footer, or no return policy page.
validate: Browser: read product page and cart DOM for return text or links; crawl the linked policy page for a live response.
action: Ask the owner to add a short return line near Add to Cart, linked to the policy.
done_when: Our re-scan finds return terms on the product page or cart.
why_it_matters: First-time shoppers from ads weigh the risk of buying; clear returns likely lift CVR.
selected_because: A trust point close to the buy button for new paid shoppers.

title: Prices shown on collection pages
group_en: Product page that converts paid traffic
group_ar: صفحة المنتج اللي بتحوّل الـ paid traffic
pass: Every product card on the collection page shows its price.
fails: Cards without a price, so shoppers must open each product.
validate: Browser: on the collection we visit, count product cards and cards with a price; screenshot. GA4: note whether paid sessions land on collection pages (landingPage for paid channels).
action: Ask the developer to show the price on every product card.
done_when: Every card on the collection shows a price in our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Collection-page campaigns lose shoppers who can't compare prices, so CVR on those clicks likely reads lower.
selected_because: Matters for campaigns that land on collections; clean DOM check.

title: Add to Cart reachable on the phone first screen
group_en: Product page that converts paid traffic
group_ar: صفحة المنتج اللي بتحوّل الـ paid traffic
pass: On a phone, Add to Cart is in the first screen of the product page or stays reachable while scrolling.
fails: Add to Cart sits several screens down below images and text.
validate: Browser (phone): record the Add to Cart button position against the viewport and whether it stays fixed on scroll; screenshot. GA4: flag high only when view_item→add_to_cart (GA4-02) is below the tool's benchmark.
action: Ask the developer to bring Add to Cart into the first screen on phone, or keep it fixed on scroll.
done_when: Our phone re-scan finds Add to Cart in the first screen or fixed on scroll.
why_it_matters: If mobile paid visitors can't see the button, fewer add to cart, so CVR likely reads lower.
selected_because: A checklist item kept only because it is tied to the GA4 product-to-cart step.

title: Cart quantity and remove controls work
group_en: Add to Cart and cart that work
group_ar: الـ Add to Cart والـ cart شغالين صح
pass: In the cart, changing the quantity updates the line and total without errors, and an item can be removed.
fails: Quantity changes don't update the total, show an error, or need a reload.
validate: Browser: after our add, raise the quantity by one in the cart, read the total before and after, then remove the item and confirm the cart updates; screenshot.
action: Send the steps to the developer to fix the cart quantity update.
done_when: Our re-scan sees the total change with the quantity and the item removed cleanly.
why_it_matters: A cart that breaks when shoppers adjust it loses orders from clicks already paid for, so CVR likely reads lower.
selected_because: A functional cart check we can run in our own visit; lowest value of the set.

title: Paid campaign that brings clicks but almost no sales
pass: No paid campaign with real session volume converts near zero in GA4 over the last 28 days.
fails: A paid campaign brings many sessions with almost no purchases; GA4 names the campaign and the landing page it sends people to.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-07: run_report 28 days, dimensions=[sessionCampaignName, sessionDefaultChannelGroup, landingPage], metrics=[sessions, transactions], paid channel groups only; rank by sessions and flag campaigns with real volume and near-zero transactions.
action: Check that campaign's landing page against the ad promise. Point the campaign to a page that sells, or pause it while the developer fixes the page.
done_when: The campaign is paused or points to a new landing page, and its GA4 conversion rate is up over the next 14 days.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks on this campaign are likely lost after landing, so CAC is higher than it needs to be; fixing the page or the destination is expected to raise ROAS on the same spend.
selected_because: Answers 'ads or site?' directly with a named campaign and landing page from the store's own GA4.

title: Each order counted once
pass: purchase event count equals transactions, and no transaction ID appears on more than one purchase event.
fails: purchase fires more than once per order (thank-you page refresh, platform app plus GTM, two tags), so GA4 shows more purchases than real orders.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days eventName=purchase metrics=[eventCount, transactions]; second run_report dimensions=[transactionId] metrics=[eventCount], count IDs with eventCount above 1 and purchases with transactionId (not set).
action: Forward to the developer: fire purchase once per order with a unique transaction_id, and block repeats when the thank-you page is refreshed or reopened.
done_when: purchase event count equals transactions over 7 days and no transaction ID repeats.
why_it_matters: Duplicate purchases make reported ROAS read higher than real, so losing campaigns can look like winners; fixing it may lower reported ROAS, which is the truth showing, not performance dropping.
selected_because: Over-count is the top 'is the number real?' failure and drives scaling into loss; decidable from GA4 transaction IDs.

title: Purchase sends a real value and currency
pass: Every purchase carries a numeric value and the store currency, and item revenue adds up to purchase revenue apart from shipping and tax.
fails: Revenue is zero or missing, currency is not sent or mixed, or item revenue does not add up to the purchase value (missing or duplicated items, value sent as text).
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days eventName=purchase metrics=[eventCount, purchaseRevenue, itemRevenue]; run_report dimensions=[currencyCode] for purchase; flag zero revenue, more than one currency, or item revenue far from purchase revenue.
action: Forward to the developer: the purchase event must send value as a number, the store currency, and the full items list.
done_when: purchaseRevenue is above zero, one currency shows on purchases, and item revenue matches purchase revenue apart from shipping and tax.
why_it_matters: Missing or wrong values make reported ROAS read lower than real, so value-based bidding learns from bad numbers and winning campaigns can get cut.
selected_because: Value and currency are what ROAS is built on; extends the current revenue check with an item-sum cross-check.

title: GA4 tag loads only once per page
pass: Each page sends one page_view and one hit per event to the store's GA4 Measurement ID, and one Add to Cart click sends one add_to_cart.
fails: gtag.js or the GA4 config loads twice (theme code plus GTM plus a platform app), so page views and events, including add_to_cart, are sent twice.
validate: Headless phone and desktop visit of home, one collection, one product and the cart: count gtag/js loads per Measurement ID and GA4 collect hits per event name in the network log; our Add to Cart click must produce exactly one add_to_cart hit.
action: Forward to the developer: keep one GA4 setup (GTM or the platform app, not both) and remove the extra snippet.
done_when: A fresh visit shows one page_view per page and one add_to_cart per click in the network log and in GA4 DebugView.
why_it_matters: Double hits make event counts and funnel rates read higher than real, so the data your campaigns are judged and retargeted on is inflated.
selected_because: Tested in CRO audits and failed on 3 of 5 stores; reproducible proof from the network log the owner can accept.

title: Where paid visitors drop after the click
pass: For paid sessions, each step (view_item to add_to_cart, add_to_cart to begin_checkout, begin_checkout to purchase) is at or above the tool's step benchmark.
fails: One step loses most paid visitors; the worst step is named with the page behind it.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[eventName, sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[totalUsers] for view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase, paid channel groups only; compare each step with the GA4-01 benchmarks and name the worst. Checkout steps come from GA4 only; the headless visit does not go past the cart.
action: Forward the worst step and its page to the owner and developer; the Conversion review lists what is wrong on that page.
done_when: That step's rate for paid sessions is up over 14 days in GA4.
why_it_matters: Closing the worst post-click step converts more of the same paid clicks, so CVR and ROAS are expected to rise and CAC to fall.
selected_because: The core 'does paid traffic convert?' answer; the four current funnel points measure one funnel, so they merge into one paid-only point.

title: UTMs and click IDs survive to the landing page
pass: A landing URL opened with test UTMs and click IDs (gclid, fbclid, ttclid, ScCid) keeps them after every redirect, and the first GA4 page_view carries them in page_location.
fails: A redirect (http to https, www, trailing slash, language or country redirect) drops the query string, or URL redaction strips UTMs and click IDs before GA4 sees them.
validate: Headless phone visit of the home page and one product URL with test utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, gclid, fbclid, ttclid and ScCid appended: record the redirect chain and final URL, and read page_location in the first GA4 collect hit.
action: Forward to the developer: keep the full query string on every redirect, and exclude UTM and click ID keys from URL redaction.
done_when: A test click URL lands with all parameters intact and GA4 DebugView shows the right source and campaign.
why_it_matters: Lost click IDs and UTMs push paid sales into Direct or Unassigned, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and the platforms match fewer conversions to clicks.
selected_because: Under-credit on every paid click is high value for the buyer and fully reproducible with a test URL.

title: Key events count only real sales
pass: purchase is a key event, and no page_view, scroll, session_start, audience-trigger or other non-sale event is.
fails: Non-sale events are marked as key events (key events: the actions GA4 counts as conversions), so conversion rates can go above 100% and imported conversions count actions that are not sales.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-20: list_key_events; flag purchase missing, any noise or audience-trigger event marked as a key event, and key events with zero count in the period.
action: Mark purchase as a key event and unmark the rest (GA4 edit access); then check which GA4 conversions Google Ads imports.
done_when: The key events list shows only real conversions and the session key event rate is below 100%.
why_it_matters: Non-sale key events make reported conversions and ROAS read higher than real, and Google Ads bids on actions that are not sales.
selected_because: Named in the persona spec as a core over-count cause; decided by code from the key events list.

title: Tracking live with no sudden drop
pass: Events flow in realtime, and sessions and purchases show no unexplained drop week on week.
fails: No live users, or sessions fell over 40% week on week, often after a site release or GTM publish.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-15: run_realtime_report activeUsers; run_report sessions and purchase eventCount for the last 7 vs the prior 7 days.
action: Ask the developer what changed in the last GTM publish or site release and restore the tag.
done_when: Realtime shows events and the week-on-week drop is explained or gone.
why_it_matters: When tracking drops, GA4 misses sales, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and good campaigns can get cut.
selected_because: A broken tag invalidates every other number; must be ruled out before judging campaigns.

title: Payment gateways taking credit for paid sales
pass: No payment gateway (Tabby, Tamara, Tap, PayTabs, a bank 3-D Secure page) shows as a session source.
fails: Gateway domains show as referral sources with purchases, taking credit from the paid campaign that brought the buyer.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-19: run_report dimensions=[sessionSource, sessionMedium] metrics=[sessions, transactions], matched against a gateway domain list.
action: Add the gateway domains to the unwanted referrals list in the GA4 data stream (whoever has GA4 edit access).
done_when: No gateway domain appears as a source with purchases over 7 days.
why_it_matters: Sales credited to a gateway are taken from your campaigns, so paid ROAS in GA4 reads lower than real.
selected_because: Common in GCC stores using BNPL; the persona spec names it directly.

title: Paid landing pages that don't convert
pass: No landing page with real paid traffic converts under a third of the store average.
fails: A landing page that gets a large share of paid sessions converts under a third of the store average.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[landingPage, sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions, transactions], paid channel groups only; compare each page with the store average (GA4-06 rule).
action: Send ad traffic to a page that converts, and forward this page to the developer with the Conversion review findings for it.
done_when: The page converts at half the store average or more, or no paid traffic lands on it.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks landing on a weak page are bought and lost, so CVR is low and CAC higher than it needs to be; fixing it is expected to raise ROAS.
selected_because: Page-level view across campaigns; the current point covers all traffic, the buyer needs paid only.

title: Paid sessions with an unknown source
pass: Unassigned and (not set) are under 10% of sessions, and paid traffic lands in a paid channel group.
fails: Over 10% of sessions have no known channel, or paid campaigns fall into Unassigned or Referral because of untagged links or mediums GA4 does not recognise.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-08: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions, transactions]; list the top source/medium pairs inside Unassigned.
action: Tag every ad, bio, WhatsApp and SMS link with UTMs; for Unassigned pairs from ad platforms, change utm_medium to a value GA4 counts as paid.
done_when: Unassigned under 5% of sessions and no ad platform source sits in Unassigned.
why_it_matters: Paid sales hidden in Unassigned are not credited to your campaigns, so paid ROAS in GA4 reads lower than real.
selected_because: Unattributed sessions hide paid results; the buyer can fix most of it in their own ad URLs.

title: Session breaks between store domains
pass: The store's own domains and checkout domain never show as a session source, and links to other store domains carry the _gl linker.
fails: The store's own domain, checkout subdomain or app domain appears as a referral source, so the session restarts and the purchase loses the campaign that brought it.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionSource, sessionMedium] metrics=[sessions, transactions], flag the store's own hostnames and checkout domains; headless visit: check whether links to other store domains get a _gl parameter.
action: Forward to the developer: set up cross-domain measurement for every store and checkout domain in the GA4 data stream, and list own domains as unwanted referrals.
done_when: No own or checkout domain shows as a source with purchases over 7 days.
why_it_matters: Each session break hands the sale to a self-referral, so paid ROAS reads lower than real and fewer purchases reach the campaign that earned them.
selected_because: Under-credit at checkout is high value for the buyer; self-referrals are readable in GA4.

title: Clean UTM names on paid links
pass: Paid source, medium and campaign values are lowercase, consistent per platform, use mediums GA4 recognises, and contain no placeholders or broken encoding.
fails: One platform appears under several spellings (Facebook, facebook, fb), mediums are invented, or values hold unresolved placeholders ({{campaign.name}}, %7B) or encoded ampersands that break the parameters after them.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionSource, sessionMedium, sessionCampaignName] metrics=[sessions, transactions]; code flags case variants of one source, placeholder patterns ({{, }}, %7B, %7D, &), mediums outside GA4's paid list, and offline values such as utm_medium=qr that land in Unassigned.
action: Fix the URL parameters in your ad templates (Meta, Snap, TikTok, Google) to one lowercase naming scheme, and check that dynamic placeholders resolve.
done_when: Each platform shows under one source/medium pair in GA4 and no placeholder values appear for 7 days.
why_it_matters: Split or broken UTM values scatter paid sales across rows and channels, so campaign ROAS in GA4 reads lower than real and winners are harder to spot.
selected_because: The buyer owns the UTMs, so this is the one GA4 fix they can make themselves today.

title: Paid traffic on phones vs desktop
pass: For paid sessions, mobile conversion is at least 60% of desktop.
fails: Paid mobile sessions convert under 60% of paid desktop sessions, with enough visits on both.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[deviceCategory, sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions, transactions], paid channel groups only (GA4-05 rule).
action: Forward the phone screenshots of the worst page to the developer, and fix the phone issues before scaling mobile placements.
done_when: Paid mobile conversion at 60% or more of paid desktop over 14 days.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks on phones that cannot convert raise CAC; fixing the phone page is expected to lift CVR and ROAS on mobile placements.
selected_because: Device gap on paid sessions points to a site problem, not an ad problem.

title: Paid sessions that look like bots
pass: No paid source, campaign or placement brings sessions with near-zero engagement and no add_to_cart, and no session spike shows without matching purchases.
fails: One paid source or placement sends many sessions with almost no engagement time and no product views, or sessions jump with no change in purchases.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionSource, sessionMedium, sessionCampaignName] metrics=[sessions, engagementRate, userEngagementDuration, addToCarts, transactions], compare each paid row with the store's paid average; run_report dimensions=[date] for 90 days to find spikes without purchases.
action: Exclude that placement, audience network or source in the ad platform, then watch engaged sessions.
done_when: The flagged source's sessions drop, or its engagement rate matches the rest of paid traffic over 14 days.
why_it_matters: Bot or junk clicks are paid for but can never buy, so CAC is higher than it needs to be and CVR reads lower than real.
selected_because: Wasted paid clicks the buyer can act on in their own ad account, found from GA4 engagement data.

title: Google Ads linked to GA4
group_ar: الـ signal اللي الحملات بتتعلم منها
pass: Google Ads is linked to this GA4 property.
fails: No Google Ads link, so GA4 audiences and conversions cannot reach Google Ads and GA4 shows no Google Ads cost.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-21: list_google_ads_links. Whether purchase is the primary conversion in Google Ads is not verifiable from the audit: check in Google Ads.
action: Link Google Ads to GA4 (needs GA4 edit and Google Ads admin access) and import purchase as the primary conversion.
done_when: The link shows in GA4 Admin and purchase is a primary conversion in Google Ads.
why_it_matters: Without the link, Google bidding and audiences miss GA4 sales data, so Smart Bidding learns from less signal; fixing it is expected to improve ROAS over time.
selected_because: Direct signal path for Google campaigns; readable from the Admin API.

title: Funnel events all fire with sane counts
group_ar: الـ signal اللي الحملات بتتعلم منها
pass: view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase all record, and begin_checkout is in line with views of the checkout page.
fails: A funnel event is missing or far too low, or begin_checkout differs a lot from checkout page views, so a trigger is broken.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-17: run_report dimensions=[eventName] metrics=[eventCount] for the ecommerce events; plus run_report dimensions=[pagePath] metrics=[screenPageViews] for checkout pages compared with the begin_checkout count.
action: Forward to the developer: add or fix the missing event so every funnel step reaches GA4.
done_when: Every funnel step shows in GA4 with counts that match views of its page.
why_it_matters: Missing funnel events mean fewer signals and smaller retargeting audiences, so the algorithm learns slower and CAC stays higher.
selected_because: Without complete events the paid funnel cannot be measured; adds a page-view cross-check to the current point.

title: Retargeting audiences ready
group_ar: الـ signal اللي الحملات بتتعلم منها
pass: Cart-abandoner or product-viewer audiences exist and Google Ads is linked.
fails: Only GA4's default audiences exist, or there is no Google Ads link to use them in.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-14: list_audiences and list_google_ads_links.
action: Create cart-abandoner and product-viewer audiences in GA4 and share them with Google Ads.
done_when: Both audiences exist and show users in Google Ads.
why_it_matters: Without these audiences you cannot retarget people who already viewed or carted from GA4 data, so retargeting reach and ROAS are lower than they could be.
selected_because: A buyer-owned lever that is readable from the Admin API.

title: Product pages that get views but no add to cart
pass: No popular product's add-to-cart rate is far below the store average.
fails: A product page with many views adds to cart at under half the store average.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-10: run_report 28 days dimensions=[pagePath, eventName] metrics=[eventCount] for view_item and add_to_cart.
action: If you run ads to this product, forward it to the owner (price, photos, stock, size info on that page), or move spend to products that add to cart.
done_when: That product's add-to-cart rate reaches the store average, or ads no longer point to it.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks sent to a product that does not add to cart are wasted, so CAC rises; fixing the page or switching the product is expected to lift CVR.
selected_because: Tells the buyer which product to stop advertising or forward for a fix.

title: Order value vs free-shipping threshold
pass: The free-shipping threshold sits at 1.1–1.6× the average order value.
fails: No threshold found on the site, or it sits below or far above the average order value.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-11: AOV from purchaseRevenue / transactions, 28 days; threshold read from the live store pages and the cart in the headless visit.
action: Ask the owner to set free shipping at about 1.3× AOV and show it in the cart.
done_when: Threshold set at 1.2–1.5× AOV and visible in the cart.
why_it_matters: A threshold just above AOV encourages bigger baskets, so AOV and ROAS are expected to rise at the same CAC.
selected_because: An AOV lever measured against this store's own GA4 AOV, not a generic best practice.

title: Countries that get visits but never buy
pass: Countries with real traffic also produce sales.
fails: A country with a real share of sessions, often from paid channels, has zero purchases.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-09: run_report 28 days dimensions=[country, sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions, transactions].
action: Exclude those countries from ad targeting, or confirm with the owner that the store ships there.
done_when: Paid sessions from those countries close to zero.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks from countries the store does not sell to cannot convert, so CAC is higher than it needs to be.
selected_because: Wasted paid clicks the buyer can stop in targeting settings.

title: Data comes only from the live store
pass: All sessions and purchases come from the store's live hostnames.
fails: Staging, preview, localhost, theme-editor or unknown hostnames send sessions or test purchases into the live property.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[hostName] metrics=[sessions, transactions, purchaseRevenue]; flag any hostname that is not the store's live domain or checkout domain.
action: Forward to the developer: send test and staging traffic to a separate GA4 property, and filter unknown hostnames.
done_when: Only live store hostnames appear in GA4 over 7 days.
why_it_matters: Test orders and unknown hostnames add purchases that never happened, so reported ROAS can read higher than real.
selected_because: Catches fake purchases in the live numbers with one hostname report.

title: Internal links that overwrite the ad source
pass: No internal link on the store carries utm_ parameters.
fails: Banners, menus or home-page sliders link to the store's own pages with UTMs, which start a new session and replace the paid source.
validate: Public crawl of home, one collection, one product and the cart: list links to the store's own domain whose href has utm_source, utm_medium or utm_campaign; GA4 cross-check: sessionSource values that match those internal tags.
action: Forward to the developer or content team: remove UTMs from internal links and use GA4 events for banner clicks.
done_when: The crawl finds no internal link with UTMs.
why_it_matters: Each internal UTM click takes the sale away from your campaign, so paid ROAS in GA4 reads lower than real.
selected_because: A hidden under-credit cause that the crawl proves link by link.

title: Hours and days that convert
pass: Conversion is about even across the day and week.
fails: Some hours or weekdays convert far better than others, with enough volume to act on.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-16: run_report 28 days dimensions=[dayOfWeek, hour] metrics=[sessions, transactions].
action: Shift budget or set an ad schedule toward the hours and days that convert, where the platform allows it.
done_when: Ad schedule or budget split set to match in the ad accounts.
why_it_matters: Spend in hours that rarely convert raises CAC; moving it is expected to lower CAC on the same budget.
selected_because: A budget decision the buyer makes alone, from the store's own GA4 data.

title: Property currency and timezone match the store
pass: Property currency and timezone match the store's main market.
fails: Currency or timezone differs from the country most sessions and sales come from, so revenue shows in another currency and days do not line up with the ad platforms or the store admin.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-22: get_property (currencyCode, timeZone), compared with the top country by sessions and transactions.
action: Set the GA4 property currency and timezone to the store's market (GA4 edit access).
done_when: Property settings show the store's currency and timezone.
why_it_matters: A wrong currency or timezone makes GA4 revenue and daily numbers disagree with Ads Manager and the store admin, so GA4 ROAS checks are off.
selected_because: Revenue currency and day boundaries decide whether GA4 and the ad platforms can be compared.

title: Each purchase counted once on every platform
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Every Purchase tag (GA4, Meta, Snap, TikTok, Google Ads) fires on the dataLayer purchase event, not on a thank-you page view, and sends the order's transaction_id.
fails: A Purchase or conversion tag fires on a page-view trigger matching the thank-you URL, so a refresh or a back-button visit sends the order again; or no transaction_id is sent, so GA4 can't drop the repeat.
validate: GTM read: list every purchase/conversion tag for each platform, its firing trigger (custom event vs page view + URL filter) and whether transaction_id (or the platform's order id) is mapped. Fail on any URL-based purchase trigger or missing order id.
action: Ask the developer to fire every Purchase tag on the dataLayer purchase event and send the order id with it.
done_when: No purchase or conversion tag in the live container uses a page-view or URL trigger, and each one sends the order id.
why_it_matters: A repeat Purchase makes reported ROAS read higher than real, so losing campaigns can look like winners and get scaled; fixing it may lower reported ROAS, which is the truth showing.
selected_because: Over-count drives scaling into loss; fully readable in the container and already a strong current-tool point.

title: Shopify checkout purchases actually reach the platforms
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: The store is not on Shopify, or begin_checkout and Purchase for each platform come from a Shopify Customer Events pixel or the platform's native Shopify app.
fails: A Shopify store relies on GTM tags for checkout and Purchase, but GTM does not run inside Shopify checkout, so those events never fire.
validate: Crawl/browser: detect Shopify. GTM read: find begin_checkout and Purchase tags and check whether they rely on triggers that can only fire inside checkout. Browser: look for the Shopify web pixel manager loading custom or app pixels on storefront pages. Checkout itself is not observed; say so.
action: Ask the developer to send checkout and Purchase from a Shopify Customer Events custom pixel or the platform's own Shopify app, not from GTM.
done_when: No platform depends on a GTM-only Purchase tag on Shopify, and a custom or app pixel for each paid platform is visible on the storefront.
why_it_matters: Sales that never fire make reported ROAS read lower than real, so winning campaigns can get cut and the algorithm learns from fewer purchases.
selected_because: A whole-store under-count on the most common platform; readable from container plus platform detection.

title: One setup per platform, no duplicate or stray pixels
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Each platform (Meta, Snap, TikTok, GA4, Google Ads) is sent by one setup only, with the store's own IDs, and no pixel from a past agency or vendor still fires.
fails: The same pixel loads from two places (platform app, Salla or Zid built-in integration, GTM, hard-coded snippet), two GA4 config tags share one ID, or an old agency's pixel ID still receives events.
validate: Browser: on home, product and cart, count base-pixel inits and PageView/AddToCart hits per platform and per pixel ID after our Add-to-Cart click; two hits for one action or two IDs for one platform fails. GTM read: count Google tag/GA4 config tags per ID, extra page_view tags, paused or triggerless tags and pixel IDs; compare with the IDs seen live.
action: Pick one setup per platform, remove the others, and delete pixels from past agencies.
done_when: Our Add-to-Cart click produces one hit per platform, each to one pixel ID the store owns.
why_it_matters: Two setups send each event twice, so reported ROAS reads higher than real; an old pixel splits signal away from the account you optimise.
selected_because: Tested in audits (2 of 3 stores failed) and visible directly in network hits.

title: Meta events carry an event_id for CAPI dedupe
group_ar: Meta: الـ Pixel والـ CAPI والـ fbclid
pass: Every Meta Purchase and AddToCart tag sends an event_id from one shared variable that the Conversions API feed can reuse, unique per event.
fails: The Pixel sends no event_id, or a fixed or reused value, so Pixel and CAPI copies of one sale can't be matched.
validate: GTM read: eventID parameter on Meta Purchase and AddToCart tags and the variable behind it (unique per event, not a constant). Browser: the eid parameter on the live AddToCart hit after our click. Whether CAPI uses the same id is not visible from here; say so.
action: Ask the developer to send a unique event_id on Meta Pixel events and pass the same id to the Conversions API.
done_when: Meta Purchase and AddToCart tags read eventID from a per-event variable, and the live AddToCart hit shows an eid.
why_it_matters: With Pixel plus CAPI and no shared event_id, Meta can count a sale twice, so reported ROAS reads higher than real.
selected_because: event_id dedupe is named in the spec; the browser side is fully checkable.

title: Purchase sends value, currency and items as data
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Every platform's Purchase and Add to Cart tag sends value as a number, the store's currency (SAR, AED, EGP and so on) and items, read from dataLayer variables that resolve.
fails: Value is missing, sent as text, or hard-typed; currency is missing or wrong; a dataLayer path is mistyped and returns undefined; items are empty.
validate: GTM read: for each platform's Purchase and Add to Cart tag, check value, currency and items/contents parameters and the dataLayer variable paths behind them (e.g. ecommerce.value, ecommerce.currency, ecommerce.items). Browser: after our Add-to-Cart click, read the dataLayer push and each pixel hit (Meta cd[value]/cd[currency], TikTok value/currency, Snap price/currency) for a numeric value and a currency.
action: Ask the developer to map value, currency and items from one set of dataLayer variables into every platform's Purchase and Add to Cart tag.
done_when: Every Purchase and Add to Cart tag reads value, currency and items from resolving variables, and our Add-to-Cart hit carries a numeric value and the store's currency on each platform.
why_it_matters: Without value and currency the platforms can't see revenue, so reported ROAS reads low or blank and value-based bidding has nothing to learn from.
selected_because: Revenue the platforms never see; checkable in config and in the live Add-to-Cart hit.

title: Consent default set first and not blocking GCC visitors
group_en: Consent that doesn't hide your sales
group_ar: الـ consent من غير ما يخبّي مبيعاتك
pass: A consent default fires on Consent Initialization before any tag, set per region: denied where the law requires it, granted where it doesn't (for example GCC and Egypt).
fails: The consent default fires late, or denies every tag in every region, so Meta, Snap, TikTok and Google tags stay silent for visitors who never touch the banner.
validate: GTM read: the consent/CMP tag's trigger (Consent Initialization - All Pages) and its default parameters, including region lists. Browser: on first load with no banner action, check whether pixel hits fire and read the consent state in Google hits (gcs/gcd).
action: Ask the developer to move the consent default to Consent Initialization and set it per region, so GCC and Egypt visits record normally.
done_when: The consent default fires before any tag, and a first visit with no banner action from a non-EEA region fires the platform pixels.
why_it_matters: Blocked tags hide real sales from every platform, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and the algorithm learns from a fraction of buyers.
selected_because: Tested in audits (2 of 4 failed the default); one config hides sales on all platforms at once.

title: Meta Pixel sends the full funnel
group_ar: Meta: الـ Pixel والـ CAPI والـ fbclid
pass: The Meta Pixel base code loads before its events, and ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout and Purchase all exist, each on the right event.
fails: Meta paid traffic shows in GA4 but the Pixel only sends PageView, Purchase is missing, or event tags fire before the base code loads and get dropped.
validate: GA4 report: sessionSource/medium for facebook, instagram, meta paid traffic. Browser: facebook.com/tr hits for PageView, ViewContent on the product page and AddToCart after our click. GTM read: Meta tags for InitiateCheckout and Purchase, their triggers, and tag sequencing or priority so the base code fires first.
action: Ask the developer to add the missing Meta events and fire the Pixel base code before them.
done_when: ViewContent and AddToCart hits are seen live, and InitiateCheckout and Purchase tags exist on the matching dataLayer events.
why_it_matters: Missing funnel events leave Meta optimising on thin signal, so delivery finds fewer buyers and CAC likely runs higher than it needs to.
selected_because: Meta leads tracked spend; base-before-events was tested (2 of 3 stores failed).

title: Tracking loads on every page your ads land on
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: The live site loads the GTM container we read on home, collection, product, cart and the top campaign landing pages from GA4.
fails: The container is missing on some templates or landing pages, or the site loads a different container ID from the one being edited.
validate: Crawl: GTM snippet and container ID in the HTML of home, one collection, one product, the cart and GA4's top campaign landing URLs. Browser: gtm.js loads with the same ID on each. GTM read: compare that ID with the container read via the service account.
action: Ask the developer to add the store's GTM container to every template, including landing pages built outside the theme.
done_when: Every checked page loads the same container ID, and it is the one the team edits.
why_it_matters: Pages with no tracking send no events, so sales from those landing pages go uncounted and reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Tested in audits (3 of 5 stores failed placement); fully crawlable.

title: Server route for Meta CAPI, Snap CAPI and TikTok Events API
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: A server-side route for ad events is visible: a server GTM container (server_container_url or transport_url), first-party collection hits, or a detected platform app that sends server events, for each paid platform.
fails: Every paid platform is browser-pixel only, so purchases blocked by ad blockers, Safari or iOS limits never reach Meta, Snap or TikTok.
validate: GTM read: server_container_url / transport_url on the Google tag, server-bound tags or templates for Meta CAPI, Snap CAPI or TikTok Events API. Browser: hits to a first-party collection subdomain. Crawl: platform app scripts that offer server events. If an app is present but its server events can't be seen, mark 'not visible from outside', not failed.
action: Ask the developer to add a server route (server GTM or each platform's server integration) for Purchase on Meta, Snap and TikTok, with the same event_id as the Pixel.
done_when: A server route is visible in the container or network for each paid platform.
why_it_matters: Browser-only tracking misses blocked sales, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and the algorithm learns from fewer buyers.
selected_because: Tested (2 of 5 stores had no server route); kept to what the container and network show, no Events Manager data.

title: Add to Cart fires only when something was added
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Add to Cart fires from the store's add-to-cart dataLayer event or the theme's AJAX add, including drawer and quick adds, and only after the item is in the cart.
fails: Add to Cart fires on a button-click or CSS-selector trigger even when nothing was added (variant not chosen, out of stock), or it misses drawer and quick adds because it waits for a form submit or page change.
validate: Browser: our real Add-to-Cart click; compare the cart contents after the click with the add_to_cart dataLayer push and each pixel's Add to Cart hit. GTM read: the add_to_cart trigger type (custom event vs click/selector/form submit).
action: Ask the developer to trigger Add to Cart from the store's add-to-cart event, not from the button click.
done_when: Our drawer add produces exactly one Add to Cart per platform, and a click that adds nothing produces none.
why_it_matters: A wrong Add to Cart count feeds the algorithm false intent, so ATC-optimised campaigns and retargeting audiences are built on clicks that weren't adds.
selected_because: Spec lists Add to Cart on the click as medium-high; our own click proves it.

title: fbclid kept as _fbc through to the cart
group_ar: Meta: الـ Pixel والـ CAPI والـ fbclid
pass: Landing with an fbclid sets the first-party _fbc cookie, it survives redirects and later pages, and Meta hits on the product and cart pages carry it.
fails: A redirect drops fbclid, the _fbc cookie is never set, or it is set with a short lifetime and gone by the cart.
validate: Browser: open a landing URL with a test fbclid; record redirects; read the _fbc cookie value and the fbc parameter on Meta hits on the product page and after our Add-to-Cart click.
action: Ask the developer to keep fbclid on redirects and let the Meta Pixel set _fbc on the first page.
done_when: The test fbclid shows in _fbc and in the Meta AddToCart hit on the cart step.
why_it_matters: Without the click ID Meta matches fewer sales to the ad that drove them, so reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Click-ID loss is a core under-count cause; the full path to the cart is headless-testable.

title: Snap Pixel sends the funnel your Snap ads need
group_en: Snapchat: Snap Pixel, CAPI and ScCid
group_ar: Snapchat: الـ Snap Pixel والـ CAPI والـ ScCid
pass: When Snapchat sends traffic, the Snap Pixel loads and sends VIEW_CONTENT, ADD_CART and PURCHASE on the right events.
fails: Snapchat paid traffic shows in GA4 but no Snap Pixel loads, or it sends only PAGE_VIEW, or PURCHASE has no tag.
validate: GA4 report: sessionSource for snapchat paid traffic; crawl for the Snap Pixel script. Browser: tr.snapchat.com hits for VIEW_CONTENT on the product page and ADD_CART after our click. GTM read: a PURCHASE tag on the purchase event.
action: Ask the developer to add the Snap Pixel with VIEW_CONTENT, ADD_CART and PURCHASE.
done_when: VIEW_CONTENT and ADD_CART hits are seen live and a PURCHASE tag exists on the purchase event.
why_it_matters: Without Snap events, Snap campaigns optimise on clicks instead of buyers, so CAC on Snap likely runs higher than it needs to.
selected_because: Snapchat leads reach in KSA; spec says score it after Meta.

title: Snap events carry a dedupe id for Snap CAPI
group_en: Snapchat: Snap Pixel, CAPI and ScCid
group_ar: Snapchat: الـ Snap Pixel والـ CAPI والـ ScCid
pass: The Snap PURCHASE (and ADD_CART) tag sends client_dedup_id from a unique per-event variable that the Snap Conversions API feed can reuse.
fails: No dedupe id, or a fixed value, so a Pixel sale and its CAPI copy can't be matched.
validate: GTM read: client_dedup_id (or the template's dedupe field) on Snap PURCHASE and ADD_CART tags and the variable behind it. Browser: the dedupe field on the live ADD_CART hit. Whether Snap CAPI sends the same id is not visible; say so.
action: Ask the developer to send a unique client_dedup_id on Snap events and the same id from Snap CAPI.
done_when: Snap PURCHASE and ADD_CART tags read a per-event dedupe id, and the live ADD_CART hit carries one.
why_it_matters: Pixel plus CAPI without a shared id can count one Snap sale twice, so Snap's reported ROAS reads higher than real.
selected_because: Snap pixel/CAPI dedupe requested for this persona; browser side checkable.

title: TikTok pixel sends the funnel your TikTok ads need
group_en: TikTok: pixel, Events API and ttclid
group_ar: TikTok: الـ Pixel والـ Events API والـ ttclid
pass: When TikTok sends traffic, the TikTok pixel loads and sends ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout and CompletePayment (or Purchase) on the right events.
fails: TikTok paid traffic shows in GA4 but no TikTok pixel loads, it sends only PageView, or the purchase event has no tag.
validate: GA4 report: sessionSource for tiktok paid traffic; crawl for the TikTok pixel script. Browser: analytics.tiktok.com hits for ViewContent on the product page and AddToCart after our click. GTM read: InitiateCheckout and CompletePayment/Purchase tags on the matching events.
action: Ask the developer to add the TikTok pixel events that are missing.
done_when: ViewContent and AddToCart hits are seen live and checkout and purchase tags exist on the matching events.
why_it_matters: Without TikTok events, TikTok optimises on clicks instead of buyers, so CAC on TikTok likely runs higher than it needs to.
selected_because: TikTok named in the persona spec; live hits prove it.

title: TikTok events carry an event_id for Events API dedupe
group_en: TikTok: pixel, Events API and ttclid
group_ar: TikTok: الـ Pixel والـ Events API والـ ttclid
pass: The TikTok purchase and AddToCart tags send an event_id from a unique per-event variable that the Events API feed can reuse.
fails: No event_id, or a fixed value, so pixel and Events API copies of one sale can't be matched.
validate: GTM read: event_id on TikTok purchase and AddToCart tags and the variable behind it. Browser: event_id on the live AddToCart hit. Whether the Events API sends the same id is not visible; say so.
action: Ask the developer to send a unique event_id on TikTok pixel events and the same id from the Events API.
done_when: TikTok purchase and AddToCart tags read a per-event event_id, and the live AddToCart hit carries one.
why_it_matters: Pixel plus Events API without a shared event_id can count one sale twice, so TikTok's reported ROAS reads higher than real.
selected_because: TikTok Events API dedupe requested for this persona; browser side checkable.

title: Google Ads conversions, gclid and Enhanced Conversions set in the tag
group_en: Google: Ads conversions and Consent Mode v2
group_ar: Google: الـ conversions والـ Consent Mode v2
pass: When Google Ads runs, a Google Ads conversion tag (or GA4 import) is present, a Conversion Linker stores gclid in _gcl_aw, and the conversion tag has Enhanced Conversions configured with hashed user-provided data.
fails: Google Ads traffic shows in GA4 but there is no conversion tag or Conversion Linker, gclid is never stored, or Enhanced Conversions is not set in the tag.
validate: GA4 report: google / cpc traffic. GTM read: awct and Conversion Linker tags and the conversion tag's user-provided-data setting. Browser: open a landing URL with a test gclid and read the _gcl_aw cookie on the cart step. The Google Ads account side is not checked; say so.
action: Ask the developer to add the Google Ads conversion tag, the Conversion Linker and Enhanced Conversions in the tag.
done_when: The container has a conversion tag with user-provided data and a Conversion Linker, and the test gclid is stored in _gcl_aw.
why_it_matters: Missing conversions or a lost gclid leave Smart Bidding with fewer sales, so Google's reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Google is the fourth platform in the spec; container and cookie are readable, account settings left out.

title: Consent Mode v2 sends all four signals
group_en: Google: Ads conversions and Consent Mode v2
group_ar: Google: الـ conversions والـ Consent Mode v2
pass: If a consent banner is used, Consent Mode v2 sends ad_storage, analytics_storage, ad_user_data and ad_personalization, each updated from the banner choice, and each tag's consent settings match the banner categories.
fails: Only the two older signals are sent, ad_user_data and ad_personalization are missing, the update never fires after a choice, or tags ignore the mapping.
validate: Browser: read the gcd/gcs parameters on Google hits before and after accepting the banner. GTM read: the consent template's four parameters and each tag's consent settings. If no banner is used, mark not applicable.
action: Ask the developer to send all four Consent Mode v2 signals and update them from the banner.
done_when: Google hits show all four signals, and their state changes after the banner choice.
why_it_matters: Without the v2 signals Google can't use or model consented visits, so conversions in Google Ads and GA4 read lower than real.
selected_because: Consent Mode v2 requested for this persona; tested in audits (3 of 5 failed the wiring); visible in network hits.

title: UTMs reach GA4 on the first page
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Opening a campaign landing URL with UTMs keeps them through any redirect, and the first GA4 page_view carries them.
fails: A redirect (language, http to https, trailing slash, app link) strips the query string, so the paid session lands in GA4 as direct or organic.
validate: Browser: open home and GA4's top campaign landing URLs with test utm_source/utm_medium/utm_campaign; record the redirect chain and final URL, and read the document location in the first GA4 hit. Fail if the UTMs are gone.
action: Ask the developer to keep the full query string on every redirect.
done_when: The test UTMs appear in the final URL and the first GA4 page_view on every checked landing URL.
why_it_matters: Paid sessions credited to direct make your campaigns look weaker in GA4 than they are, and the GA4 to Google Ads view of paid sales reads low.
selected_because: Spec names dropped UTMs on redirect as a core 'is the number real' cause; headless-testable.

title: ScCid kept through to the cart
group_en: Snapchat: Snap Pixel, CAPI and ScCid
group_ar: Snapchat: الـ Snap Pixel والـ CAPI والـ ScCid
pass: Landing with a ScCid keeps it through redirects, stores it first-party, and later Snap hits on the product and cart pages carry it.
fails: A redirect drops ScCid or nothing stores it, so the Snap click is lost after the first page.
validate: Browser: open a landing URL with a test ScCid; record redirects; read first-party cookies set by the Snap Pixel and the Snap hits on the product page and after our Add-to-Cart click for the test value.
action: Ask the developer to keep ScCid on redirects and let the Snap Pixel store it on the first page.
done_when: The test ScCid is stored and appears in the Snap ADD_CART hit.
why_it_matters: Lost ScCid means Snap credits fewer sales to your ads, so Snap's reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: ScCid named in the persona spec; headless-testable.

title: ttclid kept through to the cart
group_en: TikTok: pixel, Events API and ttclid
group_ar: TikTok: الـ Pixel والـ Events API والـ ttclid
pass: Landing with a ttclid keeps it through redirects, stores it first-party, and later TikTok hits on the product and cart pages carry it.
fails: A redirect drops ttclid or nothing stores it, so the TikTok click is lost after the first page.
validate: Browser: open a landing URL with a test ttclid; record redirects; read first-party cookies set by the TikTok pixel and the TikTok hits on the product page and after our Add-to-Cart click for the test value.
action: Ask the developer to keep ttclid on redirects and let the TikTok pixel store it on the first page.
done_when: The test ttclid is stored and appears in the TikTok AddToCart hit.
why_it_matters: Lost ttclid means TikTok credits fewer sales to your ads, so TikTok's reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: ttclid named in the persona spec; headless-testable.

title: Click-ID and analytics cookies last long enough
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: _ga, _fbc, _gcl_aw and the Snap and TikTok first-party cookies are set with a lifetime that covers a normal consideration window, and cookie variables in GTM read the right cookie names.
fails: Cookies are set by script with a short or session-only lifetime, or a GTM cookie variable points at a wrong name, so a buyer who returns days after the ad click is no longer tied to it.
validate: Browser (Chromium): after landing with test click IDs, read each cookie's expiry and whether it was set by script or by an HTTP header. GTM read: first-party cookie variables and their names compared with the cookies seen live. Safari and Firefox behaviour is not checked; say so.
action: Ask the developer to set click-ID and analytics cookies with a long first-party lifetime (server-set where possible) and fix cookie variable names.
done_when: Every checked cookie has a lifetime longer than a session, and each GTM cookie variable matches a cookie seen live.
why_it_matters: Short cookies cut the link between the ad click and a later purchase, so returning buyers show as direct and reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: High value for purchases made days after the click (I 4); cookie expiry is readable in the headless visit.

title: WhatsApp clicks tracked as a signal
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: The store has no WhatsApp or phone links, or clicks on them fire a GA4 event and a pixel event (for example Meta Contact) with the page.
fails: The site has wa.me, api.whatsapp.com or tel: links and no tag tracks them, so orders that start in WhatsApp never reach GA4 or the ad platforms.
validate: Browser: WhatsApp and tel: links found on home, product and cart. GTM read: link-click triggers on wa.me / api.whatsapp.com / tel: and the tags they fire.
action: Ask the developer to track WhatsApp and call clicks in GA4 and in each paid platform's pixel.
done_when: A click on the store's WhatsApp link fires a GA4 event and a pixel event.
why_it_matters: WhatsApp orders that never fire an event make your campaigns look like they sell less than they do, so reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Spec names WhatsApp orders that never fire as an under-count; links and triggers are both visible.

title: Accepting the banner late still credits the ad
group_en: Consent that doesn't hide your sales
group_ar: الـ consent من غير ما يخبّي مبيعاتك
pass: When a banner shows, a visitor who lands from an ad and accepts a few seconds later still gets a page_view and pixel PageView with the original UTMs and click IDs.
fails: Tags wait for consent, then fire without the landing parameters, so the session is credited to direct and the click ID is lost.
validate: Browser: open a landing URL with test UTMs and fbclid/ttclid/ScCid; wait; accept the banner; check that the first GA4 page_view and each pixel hit after accepting carry the test values. If no banner shows to our visit, mark not applicable.
action: Ask the developer to keep the landing parameters and send them with the first hits after consent.
done_when: After a late accept, the first GA4 and pixel hits carry the test UTMs and click IDs.
why_it_matters: Visitors who accept late get credited to direct, so paid campaigns look weaker than they are and reported ROAS reads low.
selected_because: A consent leak that hides paid credit; testable with one accept in the headless run.

title: Product IDs in pixels match the product
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Ecommerce tags send items with id, name, price and quantity, and the product ID in Meta, Snap, TikTok and GA4 hits is the same one the store uses for that product.
fails: Items are missing, IDs differ between platforms, or IDs are scraped from page text (DOM variables) and break on some products.
validate: Browser: on the product page and after our Add-to-Cart click, compare the IDs in Meta (content_ids), TikTok (content_id), Snap (item_ids) and GA4 (item_id) hits with the product or variant ID in the page's product data. GTM read: items mapping and any DOM Element variables used for product data.
action: Ask the developer to send one product ID, from the dataLayer, to every platform.
done_when: All four platforms show the same product ID as the page's product data for the checked product.
why_it_matters: Mismatched IDs break catalog retargeting and product-level reporting, so dynamic ads show the wrong items or none.
selected_because: Catalog ads on Meta, Snap and TikTok depend on it; comparable from live hits.

title: GA4 sees every funnel step
group_en: Google: Ads conversions and Consent Mode v2
group_ar: Google: الـ conversions والـ Consent Mode v2
pass: GA4 tags exist for view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase.
fails: One of those events has no tag or trigger, so GA4 can't show where paid visitors drop.
validate: GTM read: GA4 event tags by event name and their triggers. Browser: view_item on the product page and add_to_cart after our click in GA4 hits.
action: Ask the developer to add GA4 tags for the missing funnel events.
done_when: All four funnel events have a GA4 tag, and view_item and add_to_cart are seen live.
why_it_matters: Without every step you can't show the owner where paid traffic is lost after the click, and Google Ads gets thinner signal from GA4.
selected_because: The funnel answers 'does paid traffic convert'; readable today.

title: Purchase can fire twice for one order
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Every Purchase tag (GA4, Meta, TikTok, Snap, Google Ads) fires on a purchase custom event, not on a thank-you URL match, and sends a transaction_id / event_id taken from the order.
fails: Purchase fires on a Page View of the thank-you URL, so a refresh or a revisit of that page sends a second Purchase; no transaction_id or event_id is mapped, so nothing can drop the repeat.
validate: GTM read: for each Purchase/conversion tag, list its firing trigger (custom event vs Page View with URL contains thank-you/order-received) and whether transaction_id (GA4) and event_id (Meta/TikTok/Snap) map to an order variable. Checkout is not observed in the browser, so the verdict comes from the container only; mark 'verify one Purchase per order in Test Events'.
action: Ask the developer to move every Purchase tag to the purchase custom event and pass the order number as transaction_id and event_id.
done_when: No Purchase tag in the live container uses a URL-match trigger, and every one carries an order-based transaction_id or event_id.
why_it_matters: A second Purchase per order makes reported ROAS read higher than real, so losing campaigns can look like winners; fixing it may lower reported ROAS, which is the truth showing.
selected_because: Highest-value 'is the number real?' check in the pool; over-count drives scaling into loss.

title: Same event sent by two setups
