group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Each platform gets one hit per action: one page_view / PageView per page load, one add_to_cart / AddToCart per click.
fails: A platform app, GTM and a hard-coded snippet each send the same pixel or GA4 event, so the network log shows two or more hits (often two pixel IDs, or two GA4 config tags) for one action.
validate: Browser: on home, product and cart (phone and desktop), count collect hits per event name per platform (google-analytics collect, facebook.com/tr, analytics.tiktok.com, tr.snapchat.com, googleadservices) for one page load and for our one Add to Cart click; list each pixel/measurement ID and where it loads from (app script, GTM, inline HTML in the crawl).
action: Send the network capture to the developer and ask them to keep one setup per platform (app or GTM, not both) and remove the extra snippet.
done_when: The network log shows exactly one hit per platform per page load and per Add to Cart click.
why_it_matters: Double events inflate reported conversions and feed the algorithm a false signal, so reported ROAS reads higher than real and audiences fill with wrong people.
selected_because: Duplicate pixels are a top buyer pain, tested failing in real stores, and fully visible in the network log.

title: Pixel missing for a platform you run
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Meta, TikTok, Snap and Google Ads tags all load and send hits (not blocked) on the paid path.
fails: A platform has no pixel, or the pixel script loads but its hits fail or are blocked (CSP, script error), so that platform never sees visits or sales.
validate: Crawl HTML for pixel IDs plus browser network requests to each vendor on home, product and cart; record loaded, fired, blocked or failed per platform. Which platforms carry spend is not visible to us, so list every platform found and every one missing for the buyer to match against their accounts.
action: Tell the store owner which platform has no working pixel; the developer adds it through GTM or the platform app.
done_when: Each platform you advertise on shows its pixel hits in the network log on home, product and cart.
why_it_matters: A platform with no pixel cannot see sales, so reported ROAS reads low and its algorithm optimises blind.
selected_because: Without a working pixel no other tracking point matters for that platform; Snap and TikTok coverage is often missed.

title: Click IDs and UTMs lost on landing
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: A landing URL with utm_* plus fbclid, ttclid, ScCid and gclid keeps them after every redirect, and the pixels store them (for example _fbc cookie, GA4 hit carries the campaign).
fails: A redirect (http to https, www, language or country switch, link shortener) drops the query string, so the click ID never reaches the pixel and the sale is credited to direct or not matched to the ad.
validate: Browser: open home and the product with test utm_source/medium/campaign and test fbclid, ttclid, ScCid, gclid values; record the redirect chain and final URL, check the parameters survive, check the _fbc / _ttp / _scid / _gcl_aw cookies and the first GA4 hit's campaign fields. Gateway redirects after the cart are not checked.
action: Ask the developer to keep the full query string on every redirect (language, country, www, https).
done_when: All test click IDs and UTMs appear on the final landing URL and in the matching cookies after one visit.
why_it_matters: Lost click IDs mean the platform cannot tie the sale to the click, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and winning campaigns can get cut.
selected_because: Named in the section brief; the pool had no candidate, so the current tool's W-26 check is used.

title: Events sent without value, currency or items
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: view_item and add_to_cart (and the matching ViewContent / AddToCart pixel hits) carry value, currency and items[] / content_ids.
fails: The dataLayer or pixel hit has no value, no currency, or an empty items array, so the platform gets the event but not what it was worth.
validate: Browser: read the dataLayer ecommerce objects and the GA4 and pixel hit parameters for view_item and our add_to_cart on the product page; flag missing value, currency or items. Purchase payload is checked in GTM read (variables mapped to value, currency, items) because checkout is not observed.
action: Ask the developer to add value, currency and items to every ecommerce push and map them in each pixel tag.
done_when: Every ecommerce event on product and cart shows value, currency and items in the dataLayer and in each platform's hit.
why_it_matters: Events without value starve value-based bidding and catalogue retargeting, so reported ROAS reads low and the algorithm optimises on counts, not money.
selected_because: Value and currency gaps failed in 3 of 5 tested stores and directly bend reported revenue.

title: Value sent as text or in the wrong currency
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: value is a plain number equal to the shown price, and currency is a three-letter ISO code that matches the price the shopper sees.
fails: value arrives as a string with a symbol or a comma decimal (so it is cut or misread), or currency is lowercase, a symbol, or a different currency from the page.
validate: Browser: compare the dataLayer and pixel value/currency for view_item and add_to_cart with the price and currency shown on the product page and in the cart; flag type, format or currency mismatch.
action: Ask the developer to send value as a number and currency as the ISO code of the price shown.
done_when: value equals the shown price as a number and currency matches the page on product and cart.
why_it_matters: A wrong value or currency makes every reported sale worth the wrong amount, so reported ROAS can read high or low and value bidding learns from bad numbers.
selected_because: Distinct from 05 (presence): this checks correctness of the number the platforms optimise on.

title: Add to Cart does not add
pass: Our real Add to Cart click on the product page adds the item and the cart count updates, on phone and desktop.
fails: The click does nothing, shows an error, or the cart stays empty.
validate: Browser facts: addToCart result from our one real click on the product page (phone and desktop), with screenshot of the cart.
action: Send the screenshot to the developer to fix the Add to Cart button or the theme script behind it.
done_when: A click on Add to Cart adds the item and the cart count updates on a phone.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks that cannot add to cart cannot buy, so CVR drops and CAC rises on the same spend.
selected_because: The biggest post-click leak we can prove directly with our own click.

title: Add to Cart not sent to GA4 and pixels
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Our one Add to Cart click produces one add_to_cart in GA4 and one AddToCart hit per pixel, only after the item is in the cart.
fails: No event fires (often on drawer or quick-add), or it fires on the click even when nothing was added.
validate: Browser facts: atcEvents after our click, matched against the addToCart result; count GA4 and pixel hits produced.
action: Ask the developer to send add_to_cart on every successful add, including the drawer and quick-add, and never on a failed click.
done_when: One add_to_cart per platform appears after a successful add and none after a failed one.
why_it_matters: Missing or fake Add to Cart events distort the mid-funnel signal and retargeting audiences the algorithm uses.
selected_because: Spec scores Add to Cart signal medium-high; checked with our own click.

title: Product IDs differ between pixel and catalogue
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: The product ID in Meta/TikTok/Snap content_ids, GA4 item_id and the page's product schema SKU/ID is the same value.
fails: The pixel sends a variant ID, handle or SKU while the other sources use a different ID, so catalogue ads cannot match the viewer to the product.
validate: Browser: on the product page, compare content_ids in ViewContent / AddToCart hits with GA4 item_id and the JSON-LD sku/productID. The catalogue feed itself is not readable; mark 'confirm the feed uses the same ID in Commerce Manager'.
action: Ask the developer to send the same product ID the catalogue feed uses in every pixel.
done_when: content_ids, item_id and the schema ID are identical on the product page.
why_it_matters: Mismatched IDs quietly break dynamic product ads and catalogue retargeting, so those campaigns learn from fewer matches.
selected_because: High-impact (I4) catalogue-ad failure; the page side is fully comparable in the network log.

title: Consent setup blocks or ignores ad tags
group_en: Consent and data the platforms may reject
group_ar: الـ consent والداتا اللي المنصات ممكن ترفضها
pass: Where a banner is shown, its choice changes the consent signal (gcs/Consent Mode parameters) and ad tags follow it; no banner default blocks tags for visitors who never answer.
fails: The banner does nothing to the tags, or the default denies everything so most paid visitors are never counted.
validate: Browser: record gcs/consent parameters and which vendor hits fire before any choice, after accept and after refuse.
action: Ask the developer to connect the banner to Consent Mode and check the default state.
done_when: After accept, ad tags fire with granted consent; after refuse, no marketing tag fires; the default matches the store's policy.
why_it_matters: Over-blocking hides real sales from the platforms, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and Google modelling has less to work with.
selected_because: Consent blocking ad tags is one of the named under-count causes for this reader.

title: Main content shows late after the ad click
pass: LCP under 2.5s on the product and home page on a throttled phone.
fails: LCP over 2.5s, so paid visitors wait for the main image or headline.
validate: Browser: performance trace with mobile throttling on home and product (LCP, plus TTFB and the LCP element).
action: Ask the developer to preload the hero/product image and cut render-blocking files.
done_when: LCP under 2.5s on a phone on home and product.
why_it_matters: People who leave before the page shows never become a landing page view, so the click-to-LPV gap widens and CAC rises; ad-side LPV is not visible to us.
selected_because: Speed after the click is in the section scope; slow paid landings failed in 3 of 4 tested stores.

title: Pixel fires too late in the page load
pass: The Meta PageView and the other pixels send their first hit early in the load, not after heavy scripts or a late GTM trigger.
fails: Pixels wait for window load or a delayed GTM trigger, so visitors who leave early are never counted.
validate: Browser: on home and product (throttled phone), record the time of each platform's first hit against first paint and load; read the GTM trigger type for the base pixel tags where the container is readable.
action: Ask the developer to fire base pixels on page initialisation instead of window load.
done_when: Each platform's first hit is sent before the page finishes loading on a throttled phone.
why_it_matters: Late pixels miss early leavers, so landing page views and visits are under-counted and the click-to-LPV gap looks worse than the page alone.
selected_because: Explains part of the link-click to LPV gap, which buyers see daily but cannot diagnose.

title: Tracking tag missing on a page type
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: GTM/gtag and the pixels load on home, collection, product and cart.
fails: A template (often collection, cart or a landing template) has no tag, so visits there are not counted.
validate: Browser: gtag/GTM and pixel requests per visited page type.
action: Ask the developer to install the tag on every page template.
done_when: Tags load on home, collection, product and cart.
why_it_matters: A page with no tag breaks the funnel the platforms see, so retargeting and conversion paths lose steps.
selected_because: Coverage gap that silently under-counts paid sessions on whole page types.

title: Script errors stop tracking and the cart
pass: No JavaScript errors on product and cart that stop later dataLayer pushes or the cart from working.
fails: An error (often repeating) breaks the cart script or stops the pushes that follow it, so later events never fire.
validate: Browser: console errors on home, product and cart, matched to the dataLayer pushes and hits that follow them.
action: Send the console log to the developer to fix the erroring script.
done_when: No console errors on product and cart, and all expected events still fire.
why_it_matters: Errors cut both conversions and the events that report them, so CVR drops and reported ROAS reads low.
selected_because: One error can break both buying and counting; fully checkable in the console.

title: Personal data in page URLs
group_en: Consent and data the platforms may reject
group_ar: الـ consent والداتا اللي المنصات ممكن ترفضها
pass: No emails or phone numbers in query strings sent with pixel or GA4 hits.
fails: A form or login puts email or phone in the URL, which the pixels then pass on.
validate: Browser and crawl: scan visited URLs and the dl / page URL parameters of pixel and GA4 hits for email or phone patterns.
action: Ask the developer to send forms by POST and strip personal data from URLs.
done_when: No email or phone appears in any URL or hit parameter on the visited pages.
why_it_matters: Platforms can flag or restrict events that carry personal data in URLs, which cuts the signal campaigns optimise on; check warnings in Events Manager.
selected_because: Real link to ads: platforms can restrict events with personal data in URLs.

title: Non-standard event names
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Ecommerce events use the standard names (view_item_list, view_item, add_to_cart; ViewContent, AddToCart).
fails: Custom names (for example productView, addtocart) that the platforms do not map to standard events.
validate: Browser: list event names in the dataLayer and in pixel/GA4 hits on collection, product and cart; flag non-standard names.
action: Ask the developer to rename events to the platforms' standard names.
done_when: All ecommerce events seen use standard names.
why_it_matters: Custom names are not used for standard optimisation or reports, so the algorithm gets a thinner funnel signal.
selected_because: Failed in 3 of 5 tested stores; directly limits what platforms can optimise on.

title: Sold-out products where paid visitors land
pass: No sold-out product in the hero or first row of home and collections.
fails: Sold-out items are featured where shoppers look first.
validate: Browser: stock state of products in the hero and first row of home and the visited collection.
action: Ask the store owner to swap sold-out items out of featured spots; pause ads pointing at them.
done_when: Every featured product on home and collections is in stock.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks on products that cannot be bought are wasted, so CAC is higher than it needs to be right now.
selected_because: Wasted paid clicks the buyer can act on at once by pausing ads.

title: Item fields use old or platform names
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: items[] use item_id, item_name, item_brand, item_category, item_variant, price, quantity.
fails: Legacy or platform-native field names (id, name, product_id) that GA4 drops, leaving item reports as (not set).
validate: Browser: read item field names in dataLayer ecommerce objects on product and cart.
action: Ask the developer to map the platform's item output to the GA4 item fields in GTM.
done_when: All items show the standard field names in the dataLayer.
why_it_matters: Dropped item data blanks product reports and the audiences built from them, which weakens product-level signal.
selected_because: Common platform quirk; readable directly in the dataLayer.

title: Old cart items attached to new events
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: ecommerce is set to null before each new ecommerce push.
fails: No clearing, so items from an earlier push merge into the next event.
validate: Browser: dataLayer sequence on product then cart; check for ecommerce:null before each push and for items carried over.
action: Ask the developer to clear the ecommerce object before each push.
done_when: Each ecommerce push follows an ecommerce:null and carries only its own items.
why_it_matters: Carried-over items inflate item counts and values on later events, so product-level numbers read higher than real.
selected_because: Over-count source visible in the dataLayer sequence.

title: Embedded widgets that hide conversions
group_en: Tracking seen in the page and network
group_ar: التتبع زي ما بيظهر في الصفحة والـ network
pass: Any iframe that takes an action on the visited pages (form, booking, embedded checkout) passes its events to the parent page's dataLayer.
fails: The action happens inside an iframe, so GA4 and the pixels on the page never see it.
validate: Browser: list iframes on home, product and cart and their domains; where one is a form or checkout, check for postMessage pushes into the parent dataLayer. Checkout after the cart is not checked.
action: Ask the developer to relay iframe events to the page's dataLayer.
done_when: Actions inside the iframe show as dataLayer events on the parent page.
why_it_matters: Conversions inside iframes never reach the platforms, so reported ROAS reads low for campaigns that drive them.
selected_because: High-impact (I4) under-count cause; iframe presence on visited pages is checkable.

title: WhatsApp and call links broken
pass: wa.me and tel: links use a full international number, or there are none.
fails: A WhatsApp or phone link with a missing or malformed number.
validate: Browser facts: contact links found on visited pages and their numbers.
action: Ask the store owner to fix the WhatsApp number in the store settings or theme.
done_when: Every WhatsApp/phone link opens a chat or call to the right full number.
why_it_matters: In COD and WhatsApp-heavy stores a broken link loses paid visitors who wanted to order by chat, so CVR drops.
selected_because: WhatsApp ordering matters in GCC paid traffic; checked directly.

title: Product schema price or stock wrong
pass: Product pages carry Product + Offer schema whose price and availability equal what the page shows.
fails: Schema missing price or availability, or showing a different price or stock than the page.
validate: Crawl: JSON-LD Product/Offer on the product page vs the visible price and stock.
action: Ask the developer to make the schema use the live price and stock.
done_when: Schema price and stock match the visible page.
why_it_matters: Google Shopping can disapprove products whose page data disagrees, which cuts Shopping and Performance Max reach.
selected_because: Real link to Google Shopping ads approval.

title: Failed or hanging requests on landing pages
pass: No 404/500 requests and no request over 3 seconds blocking content on home, product or cart.
fails: Images or scripts fail, or a slow request holds back what the shopper sees.
validate: Browser: network log status codes and durations on home, product and cart.
action: Ask the developer to fix or remove the failing and slow requests.
done_when: No 404/500 and no blocking request over 3 seconds on those pages.
why_it_matters: Broken or stalled pages lose paid visitors before they act, so CVR drops on the same clicks.
selected_because: Post-click leak visible in the network log.

title: Blocking and heavy code on first load
pass: No render-blocking CSS/JS in the head, and JS + CSS on first load under about 1 MB.
fails: Blocking files delay first paint, or the first load carries more code than the budget.
validate: Browser: performance trace (render-blocking resources) and transfer size of JS and CSS on home and product.
action: Ask the developer to defer non-critical scripts and trim unused code.
done_when: No render-blocking files and first-load JS + CSS under about 1 MB.
why_it_matters: Heavy first loads slow the page after the click, so more paid visitors leave before the landing page view.
selected_because: Main fixable cause behind slow paid landings.

title: Third-party apps slow the page
pass: Chat, review and popup apps load light or after the main content.
fails: Third-party app scripts make up most of the load weight.
validate: Browser: transfer size and timing by third-party domain on home and product.
action: Ask the store owner to remove unused apps and the developer to load the rest after the main content.
done_when: Third-party apps no longer dominate load weight on home and product.
why_it_matters: App weight slows the page after the ad click, so CVR drops and the click-to-LPV gap widens.
selected_because: Common speed leak on app-heavy stores; measured per domain.

title: Customers can see they can pay with mada, Apple Pay, Tabby or Tamara before checkout
pass: On the phone product page (near Add to cart) and in the cart, the payment methods the store accepts are shown as logos or text: mada, Apple Pay, Tabby, Tamara, STC Pay, cash on delivery, as offered.
fails: No payment logos on the product page or cart, or only Visa/Mastercard shown, so a shopper who wants mada or instalments only finds out at checkout or leaves.
validate: Headless phone and desktop visit of the product page and the cart: search the DOM (img alt/src, svg titles, class names, visible text) for mada, Apple Pay, Visa, Mastercard, STC Pay, Tabby, Tamara and cash-on-delivery wording; record which appear and whether they sit in the first screen near Add to cart and near the cart's checkout button. Screenshot both. Payment setup itself is not visible to us: mark 'confirm with owner' for methods offered but not shown.
action: Show the payment logos you accept (mada, Apple Pay, Tabby, Tamara, cash on delivery) under the Add to cart button and next to the checkout button in the cart. Most themes have a payment-icons setting or block for this.
done_when: On a phone, the product page and the cart both show the payment methods you accept without scrolling past the buy button.
why_it_matters: Shoppers who don't see their way to pay stop before checkout, so the sale is lost after they already chose the product.
selected_because: Top store-owner leak in the spec (payment visibility), Elevr list item, tested in CRO audits, owner can fix in the admin.

title: Delivery cost is shown before checkout
pass: The product page or the cart states the delivery cost (or how it is worked out, by city or order value), so the shopper knows the full price before checkout.
fails: The cart says delivery is calculated at checkout or says nothing, and no delivery-cost text is reachable from the product page; the cost first appears at the last step.
validate: Headless phone visit of product page and cart after our add to cart: search visible text for delivery/shipping cost wording (توصيل, شحن, delivery, shipping) with an amount or a rule; note 'calculated at checkout' wording. Public crawl of the delivery/shipping policy page linked from the footer to see if costs are listed. Screenshot cart.
action: Write the delivery cost in the cart and on the product page (for example the price per city or 'free above X'), and keep the delivery policy page linked from both.
done_when: A phone shopper can read the delivery cost on the product page or in the cart before tapping checkout.
why_it_matters: A delivery cost that appears only at the last step is a common reason buyers drop out after adding to cart.
selected_because: Spec ranks late shipping cost high for this reader; tested and failed in 3 of 5 audited stores; owner setting.

title: Free-delivery threshold is shown and explained
pass: If the store offers free delivery above an amount, that amount is stated on the home page bar or product page, and the cart tells the shopper how much more they need to add.
fails: Free delivery is offered but the amount is not shown, the bar says 'free delivery' with no amount, or the cart gives no 'add X more' message.
validate: Headless phone visit of home, product and cart: search visible text for free-delivery wording (توصيل مجاني, شحن مجاني, free delivery/shipping) and capture any amount next to it; in the cart (with our one product) check for a remaining-amount message or progress bar. Crawl the delivery policy page for the threshold. If no free-delivery offer is found anywhere, mark 'not offered or not shown, confirm with owner'.
action: State the free-delivery amount in the top bar and on the product page, and turn on a cart message that shows how much more the customer needs to add.
done_when: Home or product page shows the free-delivery amount and the cart shows the remaining amount for the current order.
why_it_matters: A clear free-delivery amount gives shoppers a reason to add one more item, which raises order value.
selected_because: Elevr list item and a high-scoring delivery lever in the spec; visible storefront fact.

title: Cash-on-delivery fee is stated before checkout
pass: If cash on delivery is offered, the product page, cart or delivery policy page says whether it has a fee and how much.
fails: Cash on delivery is mentioned but the fee is not, so the shopper meets an extra charge at the last step; or COD wording only appears inside checkout.
validate: Headless phone visit of product page and cart plus public crawl of the delivery/payment policy pages: search for COD wording (الدفع عند الاستلام, cash on delivery, COD) and, where found, for a fee amount or 'no fee' wording near it. If COD wording is not found, mark 'COD offer not visible, confirm with owner'. We do not open checkout.
action: Add one line near the payment logos and in the delivery policy: 'Cash on delivery: fee X' or 'Cash on delivery with no extra fee'.
done_when: The COD fee (or 'no fee') is readable on the product page, the cart or the linked delivery page.
why_it_matters: An unexpected COD fee at the last step makes buyers abandon or refuse the order at the door.
selected_because: Elevr list item; spec scores hidden COD fee high; checkable from storefront text and policy pages.

title: WhatsApp button is visible on the phone
pass: On the phone product page and cart, a WhatsApp (or other contact) button is visible, opens a working wa.me or WhatsApp link, and does not cover Add to cart or the checkout button.
fails: No WhatsApp link at all, the link is only in the footer, the button is hidden on mobile, or it sits on top of the buy button.
validate: Headless phone visit of product page and cart: find links to wa.me, api.whatsapp.com or whatsapp:// and chat widgets; check the element's box is inside the viewport and visible, and that it does not overlap the Add to cart or checkout button boxes. Record the phone number format. Also note other contact routes (phone, email) in header/footer. Screenshot.
action: Turn on the floating WhatsApp button for mobile and place it so it does not cover the Add to cart or checkout buttons.
done_when: On a phone, a WhatsApp button shows on the product page and cart, opens your number, and leaves the buy buttons clear.
why_it_matters: GCC shoppers ask questions on WhatsApp before buying; a hidden button turns those questions into lost orders.
selected_because: Elevr list item and spec high-score item on mobile-heavy stores; tested (2 of 5 failed); owner setting.

title: Add to cart is in the first phone screen
pass: On a 375px phone, the product page shows the price and the Add to cart button without scrolling, or a sticky Add to cart appears as soon as the shopper scrolls.
fails: Add to cart sits below a tall gallery, banners or long text, so the shopper has to scroll to find how to buy.
validate: Headless phone visit (375px) of the product page: locate the Add to cart button and the price, read their bounding boxes and check they fall inside the first viewport; scroll once and check for a sticky buy bar. Screenshot the first screen.
action: Move the price and Add to cart up under the first product photo, or turn on the theme's sticky Add to cart bar for mobile.
done_when: A 375px screenshot of the product page shows the price and Add to cart (or a sticky bar) without scrolling.
why_it_matters: When the buy button is out of sight on a phone, fewer product visitors add to cart.
selected_because: Direct lever on product page to add to cart; tested (2 of 5 failed); measured exactly by the phone visit.

title: Product titles are in Arabic
pass: On the Arabic store, product titles on the collection page and the product page are written in Arabic (brand or model names in Latin letters are fine).
fails: Arabic pages show English-only product titles, or titles copied from the supplier with codes and no Arabic name.
validate: Headless visit of the Arabic version of the collection and product pages: read the product card titles and the product h1; compute the share of titles that contain Arabic letters; list the English-only titles found.
action: Add an Arabic title to each product in the product editor, starting with your best-selling products; keep the brand name as is.
done_when: All product titles on the Arabic collection page and the opened product page contain an Arabic name.
why_it_matters: Arabic-speaking shoppers find and trust products faster when the name is in their language.
selected_because: Elevr list item; spec scores Arabic product titles high; owner fixes in the product editor.

title: Arabic pages read right to left on the phone, cart included
pass: Arabic pages declare lang=ar and dir=rtl, and the product page and cart lay out right to left on a phone: prices, quantity, remove and checkout buttons in the right places with no overlapping or cut text.
fails: Arabic text inside a left-to-right layout, mirrored icons, prices or numbers jumbled, or cart rows that overlap or cut off on a phone.
validate: Headless phone visit of the Arabic home, product and cart pages: read html lang/dir and the computed direction of the main product and cart containers; check for elements whose boxes overflow the viewport or overlap in the cart; screenshot the cart for review.
action: Ask your developer or theme support to fix the right-to-left layout on the product page and cart for Arabic.
done_when: Arabic product page and cart screenshots on a phone show a correct right-to-left layout with nothing overlapping.
why_it_matters: A broken Arabic cart makes the store look unsafe at the moment the customer decides to pay.
selected_because: Spec scores RTL breaks in the cart high on mobile-heavy stores; the current tool already reads lang/dir.

title: Cart shows the same price and a clear total
pass: After adding our product, the cart shows the same price as the product page, a clear subtotal or total, and says whether delivery and VAT are included.
fails: The cart price differs from the product page, the discount shown on the product page is missing in the cart, or the total is unclear about delivery and VAT.
validate: Headless phone visit: record the price (and any sale price) on the product page, add the product to the cart, then read the cart line price, subtotal and total and any 'VAT included' or delivery wording. Flag any mismatch between product page and cart prices. Screenshot.
action: Check the product's price and discount settings so the cart shows the same price, and add a line under the total saying whether VAT and delivery are included.
done_when: Product page price equals the cart line price, and the cart total states what it includes.
why_it_matters: A price that changes between the product page and the cart breaks trust right before checkout.
selected_because: Hidden or changing total is a known cart leak; we add one product so the comparison is exact. Covers the measurable part of the Elevr 'coupon vs cart price' item.

title: Checkout button in the cart is clear on the phone
pass: The cart has one clear checkout button visible on a phone without scrolling (or sticky), with a plain label such as 'إتمام الطلب'.
fails: The checkout button is below the fold, looks like a secondary link, competes with several other buttons, or the label is unclear.
validate: Headless phone visit of the cart after our add to cart: locate the checkout button, read its label and bounding box, check it is in the first viewport or sticky, and count other buttons of equal weight. Screenshot.
action: Make the checkout button the main button in the cart and keep it visible on mobile (sticky if the cart is long).
done_when: A phone screenshot of the cart shows the checkout button without scrolling.
why_it_matters: People who already added to cart need an obvious next step, or they leave the cart without buying.
selected_because: Direct cart-to-checkout lever, the step store owners lose most; measured exactly in the cart visit.

title: Pay-in-instalments price is shown on the product page
pass: If the store offers Tabby or Tamara, the product page shows the instalment line under the price (for example 'or 4 payments of X'), and the cart shows it too.
fails: Tabby or Tamara is offered at checkout but no instalment line shows on the product page or cart, or the widget loads empty.
validate: Headless phone visit of product page and cart: look for Tabby or Tamara widget elements or scripts in the DOM and network, and for instalment text near the price; check the widget renders text, not an empty box. If no BNPL is found, mark 'not visible, confirm with owner whether Tabby or Tamara is active'.
action: Turn on the Tabby or Tamara product-page widget from the app or payment settings so the instalment amount shows under the price.
done_when: The product page and cart show the instalment line with an amount on a phone.
why_it_matters: Seeing a smaller instalment amount helps shoppers commit to higher-priced items.
selected_because: Elevr list (Tabby/Tamara on product and cart); distinct from logos because it shows the instalment amount; visible in DOM and network.

title: Phone layout has no sideways scroll and buttons are easy to tap
pass: Home, collection, product and cart pages fit the phone width with no sideways scroll; Add to cart, quantity, menu and checkout targets are 44px or more.
fails: Pages scroll sideways, or the buy, quantity or remove buttons are too small to tap.
validate: Headless 375px visit of the four pages: compare document scrollWidth with viewport width; measure the bounding boxes of Add to cart, quantity controls, menu and checkout buttons against 44px; list failures with screenshots.
action: Ask your developer to remove the element causing sideways scroll and enlarge the small buy and quantity buttons on mobile.
done_when: No sideways scroll on the four pages and all listed buttons measure 44px or more.
why_it_matters: Most store visits are on phones; missed taps and a wobbling page lose buyers on the way to the cart.
selected_because: Mobile usability on the buying path; current tool already measures it; merged with tap-size and mobile readability candidates.

title: Delivery time is shown before buying
pass: The product page (or collection cards) states how long delivery takes, in days or by city.
fails: No delivery time anywhere before checkout, or only inside a policy page that is not linked from the product page.
validate: Headless phone visit of collection and product pages: search visible text for delivery-time wording (توصيل خلال, أيام, delivery in, days) with a number; crawl the linked delivery policy page for times. Screenshot.
action: Add a short line under the price: 'Delivery in X to Y days' (by city if it differs).
done_when: The product page shows a delivery time on a phone.
why_it_matters: Shoppers who don't know when the order arrives hesitate, especially for gifts and occasions.
selected_because: Delivery expectation is a GCC trust moment; tested (3 of 5 failed); owner can add text.

title: Return and exchange policy is easy to find
pass: A return/exchange policy is linked from the footer on all pages and mentioned near Add to cart, the page loads, and it is in Arabic; privacy and terms pages are linked too.
fails: No return policy link, a broken policy page, an English-only policy on the Arabic store, or return terms only revealed after purchase.
validate: Headless visit and public crawl: find footer links to return/exchange, privacy and terms pages on home, product and cart; fetch each and check status 200 and Arabic text; search the product page for return wording near Add to cart.
action: Publish a short Arabic return and exchange policy, link it in the footer, and add one line near Add to cart (for example 'Exchange within X days').
done_when: Footer links to return, privacy and terms pages work, and the product page mentions returns near the buy button.
why_it_matters: Clear return terms reduce the fear of buying from a store the shopper doesn't know yet.
selected_because: Spec lists returns as a medium product-page trust lever; merged policy-link candidates into one point.

title: Reviews and ratings show on product and collection pages
pass: The product page shows real customer reviews with a rating and count near the title, the rating links to the reviews, and collection cards show stars where reviews exist.
fails: No reviews block, a widget showing zero reviews, a rating that doesn't link to the reviews, or reviews only in English on the Arabic store.
validate: Headless visit of product and collection pages: detect review widgets and rating elements (stars, counts) in the DOM; read the review count; check the rating links or scrolls to the review section; check review text language. Screenshot.
action: Turn on product reviews, show the rating under the product title, and ask recent buyers for a review (WhatsApp works well).
done_when: The product page shows a rating with a count under the title, and collection cards show stars.
why_it_matters: Reviews from other buyers are what convinces a hesitant first-time shopper to add to cart.
selected_because: Product-page trust (medium in spec); tested in CRO audits; merged four review candidates.

title: Product page has several clear photos
pass: The product page gallery has more than one photo (different angles, in use or with size reference), and the photos load sharp on a phone.
fails: A single photo, the same photo repeated, or blurry or broken images.
validate: Headless phone visit of the product page: count unique gallery image URLs, read their natural sizes against displayed sizes, and check for failed image requests. Screenshot the gallery.
action: Upload extra photos for each product: different angles, the product in use and a size reference.
done_when: The opened product shows more than one distinct sharp photo on a phone.
why_it_matters: Shoppers can't touch the product; more photos answer their doubts and lead to more add to carts.
selected_because: Highest-scoring tested pool candidate; owner fixes in the product editor; directly measurable.

title: Product description answers buyer questions, in Arabic
pass: The product page has an Arabic description that covers what the shopper needs to decide: size or dimensions, material or ingredients, how to use, what is in the box.
fails: Empty or one-line description, supplier text in English on the Arabic store, or key facts (size, material) missing.
validate: Headless visit of the Arabic product page: extract the description text, measure its length, check the share of Arabic letters, and look for size/material/usage terms; the model reviews the text against the product type.
action: Rewrite the description of your top products in Arabic with size, material, how to use and what's included.
done_when: The opened product's description is in Arabic and states size, material and use.
why_it_matters: Missing details make shoppers leave to ask or to buy elsewhere.
selected_because: Spec lists missing Arabic description as medium; tested (3 of 5 failed); merged two description candidates.

title: Sale price and saving are clear
pass: Prices show on every collection card, and discounted products show the old and new price (and the saving) on the card, product page and cart.
fails: Price missing on cards, old price shown without the new one, or a discount shown on the card but not on the product page or cart.
validate: Headless visit of collection and product pages: check each card has a price; where a compare-at or crossed-out price exists, check the new price and saving appear on the product page and again in the cart after our add to cart.
action: Set the old price (compare-at price) on discounted products so the saving shows everywhere, and keep the price visible on all product cards.
done_when: Every collection card shows a price, and a discounted product shows old and new price on card, product page and cart.
why_it_matters: A clear saving gets deal-seeking shoppers to act; an unclear price makes them doubt the offer.
selected_because: Price clarity is a medium spec item; tested; owner admin setting.

title: Sold-out products don't block the shopper
pass: Sold-out products and sizes are clearly marked, sit after in-stock items on the collection page, and a sold-out product page offers similar items or a 'notify me'.
fails: Many sold-out products at the top of the collection, sold-out sizes selectable until the cart, or a sold-out page with no way forward.
validate: Headless visit of the collection page: count cards marked sold out and their positions; on the product page read variant availability (disabled options, out-of-stock text) and check for similar-product or notify-me blocks.
action: Hide or move sold-out products to the end of collections, and add 'similar products' or 'notify me' on sold-out pages.
done_when: The first row of the collection has no sold-out items, and sold-out pages show alternatives.
why_it_matters: Shoppers who land on sold-out items, often from ads, leave instead of buying something else.
selected_because: Stock problems lose ready buyers; owner manages stock; visible on collection and product pages.

title: Language switch and prices in the right currency
pass: A language switch (Arabic/English) is easy to find on the phone, and prices show in the store currency (for example SAR) the same way on product, cart and collection; if a currency switch exists it works.
fails: No language switch, the switch hidden deep in the menu, prices in a different currency than the store sells in, or mixed currencies between pages.
validate: Headless phone visit of home, collection, product and cart: find language and currency switch controls in header or menu and their visibility; read the currency symbol or code on prices on each page and check they match; follow the language switch link and check the Arabic/English page loads.
action: Show the language switch in the mobile header and set prices to show in your store currency on every page.
done_when: Language switch visible on the phone header, and the same currency on collection, product and cart.
why_it_matters: Shoppers who can't read the page in their language or see a strange currency don't buy.
selected_because: Elevr list item (currency and language switching); tested (3 of 5 failed); platform setting.

title: Related products shown to raise order value
pass: The product page or cart shows related or complementary products that can be added in one tap.
fails: No related products on the product page or cart, or a block that shows the same product or sold-out items.
validate: Headless visit of product page and cart: detect related/recommended product blocks (section headings such as منتجات مشابهة, recommendation app scripts) and count in-stock items in them.
action: Turn on the related-products section on product pages and a 'you may also like' block in the cart.
done_when: Product page and cart each show at least one in-stock related product.
why_it_matters: Suggesting a matching item lets buyers add more to the same order.
selected_because: Order-value lever; tested (4 of 5 lacked tools); owner app or theme setting.

title: Search is easy to find on the phone
pass: A search icon or field is visible in the phone header on home and collection pages.
fails: No search on mobile, or search hidden inside the menu.
validate: Headless phone visit of home and collection: locate search inputs or search icons in the header and check they are visible in the first viewport.
action: Turn on the search icon in the mobile header in your theme settings.
done_when: Search shows in the phone header on home and collection pages.
why_it_matters: Shoppers who know what they want buy faster when they can search for it.
selected_because: Product-finding lever, tested (2 of 5 failed); simple theme fix.

title: Filter and sort are available on phone collection pages
pass: The collection page on a phone has visible filter and sort controls (including price), reachable without scrolling the whole list.
fails: Filters exist on desktop only, or there is no way to sort or filter on mobile.
validate: Headless phone visit of the collection page: find filter and sort controls and check they are visible in the first viewport or a sticky bar; note whether a price filter exists. Compare with desktop.
action: Turn on mobile filters and sort for collections in the theme, including a price filter.
done_when: A phone screenshot of the collection shows filter and sort controls.
why_it_matters: On large collections, shoppers who can't narrow down give up before finding a product.
selected_because: Mobile product finding on collection pages; tested; theme setting.

title: No heavy autoplay video on the phone first screen
pass: The phone home page first screen shows products or an image, not an autoplay video.
fails: An autoplay video fills the phone first screen, delaying the page and pushing products down.
validate: Headless phone visit of the home page: detect video elements with autoplay in the first viewport and record their file size from network requests. Screenshot.
action: Replace the mobile hero video with an image, or set the video to play only on tap.
done_when: The phone home page first screen has no autoplay video.
why_it_matters: A heavy video slows the first screen on mobile data, and slower pages lose visitors before they see a product.
selected_because: Current-tool point with a real mobile sales effect; owner can change the banner.

title: Menu and footer links work, and the not-found page offers a way back
pass: All menu and footer links open a working page, and the not-found page shows search or links back to products.
fails: Dead menu or footer links (old collections, deleted products), or a not-found page with no way back.
validate: Public crawl: fetch every menu and footer link from the home page and record non-200 responses; fetch a made-up URL and check the not-found page has search or product links.
action: Fix or remove the dead links listed and add search and a 'back to shop' link on the not-found page.
done_when: Crawl finds no broken menu or footer links and the not-found page links back to products.
why_it_matters: A shopper who hits a dead link often leaves the store instead of looking further.
selected_because: Current-tool point that keeps shoppers on the path; owner fixes links in the admin.

title: The one step losing you the most sales
group_ar: وين تضيع مبيعاتك في مسار الشراء
pass: Each step (product view to add to cart, add to cart to checkout, checkout to purchase) is at or above the tool's benchmark (8% / 50% / 50%).
fails: One step is below its benchmark; the worst one, with the most lost sales, is named with its page.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days, dimensions=[eventName], metrics=[totalUsers] for view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase; compare each step with 8% / 50% / 50%; money = sessions at that step x gap x average order value, in the property currency.
action: Start with the page behind the worst step. The page review below shows what your customers see there and what to change.
done_when: That step is within 10% of its benchmark over 14 days in GA4.
why_it_matters: Fixing the single worst step brings back the most sales for the least work.
selected_because: Money-first headline finding straight from the owner's own GA4; CHK-C-027 is the same step-ratio check.

title: Shoppers who start checkout but don't pay
group_ar: وين تضيع مبيعاتك في مسار الشراء
pass: At least half of started checkouts end in a purchase.
fails: Fewer than half of started checkouts are paid; add_shipping_info and add_payment_info show whether delivery or payment is where they stop.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days, metrics=[totalUsers] for begin_checkout, add_shipping_info, add_payment_info, purchase; name the sub-step with the biggest drop.
action: Place one test order on your phone. Check that the delivery cost shows before the last step, cash on delivery and its fee are clear, mada, Apple Pay, Tabby or Tamara are offered, and no account is forced.
done_when: Each item on that list is checked and fixed or ruled out, and checkout to purchase is at 50% or more over 14 days.
why_it_matters: These people already chose to buy; every one lost here is a sale you almost had.
selected_because: Highest-intent leak and it maps to GCC payment and COD fixes the owner can make in the admin.

title: Carts that never reach checkout
group_ar: وين تضيع مبيعاتك في مسار الشراء
pass: At least half of the people who add to cart start checkout.
fails: Fewer than half of shoppers with a full cart start checkout.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days, metrics=[totalUsers] for add_to_cart and begin_checkout; our cart visit (browser) shows what the cart page shows on a phone.
action: Fix what the cart review found: show the delivery cost and free-delivery threshold, payment options and a clear checkout button in the cart.
done_when: Cart to checkout is at 50% or more over 14 days.
why_it_matters: People leave full carts when the cost or next step is unclear, so sales stop one click from checkout.
selected_because: Core funnel fact, measurable today, fix sits in the owner's cart and delivery settings.

title: Product visits that don't turn into add to cart
group_ar: وين تضيع مبيعاتك في مسار الشراء
pass: At least 8 in 100 product viewers add to cart.
fails: Fewer than 8 in 100 people who open a product add it to the cart.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days, metrics=[totalUsers] for view_item and add_to_cart.
action: Fix the product page first named in this report: price, photos, Arabic title and description, delivery time and stock.
done_when: Add-to-cart rate from product views is up over 14 days in GA4.
why_it_matters: Most product visits end without a sale, so this step limits every sale after it.
selected_because: Top-of-funnel money step; fix is content the owner controls.

title: Phone shoppers buy less than desktop shoppers
group_ar: وين تضيع مبيعاتك في مسار الشراء
pass: Phone conversion is at least 60% of desktop conversion.
fails: Phones convert at under 60% of desktop while most visits come from phones.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days, dimensions=[deviceCategory], metrics=[sessions,transactions]; phone screenshots from our headless visit show the page.
action: Fix the phone issues the page review found on the worst step's page: Arabic layout, buttons, delivery and payment info on small screens.
done_when: Phone conversion is at 60% or more of desktop over 14 days.
why_it_matters: Most of your visitors are on phones, so a weak phone page holds back most of your sales.
selected_because: GCC traffic is mobile-heavy; the spec scores mobile and RTL gaps high.

title: Your sales number in GA4 matches your real orders
pass: Purchase events equal transactions, no order ID is counted twice, and every purchase has a value and currency.
fails: Purchases and transactions differ by over 10%, the same order ID appears more than once (thank-you page refresh), revenue is zero, or currency is missing.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report eventName=purchase metrics=[eventCount,transactions,purchaseRevenue]; new query: run_report 28 days dimensions=[transactionId] metrics=[eventCount] filtered to purchase, count IDs with more than one event.
action: Ask your developer to send each order to GA4 once, with its order ID, value and currency.
done_when: Purchases equal transactions, no repeated order IDs, and GA4 revenue matches your store admin within 5% for the same days.
why_it_matters: Every money figure in this report comes from this number; if it is wrong, you can't trust any of them.
selected_because: Money numbers must be believable (ICP N2); duplicate order IDs are the same failure, now checked directly.

title: GA4 is recording right now, with no sudden drops or jumps
pass: Visitors show in realtime, and week-on-week visits have no unexplained fall or one-source spike.
fails: No live users, visits fell over 40% week on week, or one day has a jump from one source or country with almost no engaged visits (likely bots).
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_realtime_report activeUsers; run_report sessions last 7 vs prior 7 days; new query: run_report 28 days dimensions=[date,sessionSource,country] metrics=[sessions,engagedSessions] to flag single-day spikes with near-zero engagement.
action: If tracking stopped, ask your developer to check the last site or app change. If a spike is bots, have it excluded so your conversion rate shows real shoppers.
done_when: Realtime shows visitors, and the last 28 days have no unexplained cliff or bot spike.
why_it_matters: A tracking gap hides sales, and fake visits make your conversion rate look worse than it is.
selected_because: Without live, clean data no other finding holds; bot and volume-jump checks are the same stability question.

title: Every buying step is recorded
pass: Product view, add to cart, begin checkout and purchase all record with believable counts.
fails: A step is missing, or so low (under 30% of benchmark) that it is likely not recording.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[eventName] metrics=[eventCount] for view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase; our headless add-to-cart click confirms whether add_to_cart fires.
action: Ask your developer, or your store's GA4 app, to send the missing step so you can see where shoppers stop.
done_when: All four steps show in GA4 with believable counts.
why_it_matters: You can't find where sales are lost if a step of the path isn't recorded.
selected_because: Prerequisite for every funnel money figure; measurable today.

title: Your store sends every visit and order to GA4 twice
pass: One GA4 tag per page: each page load sends one page_view per GA4 measurement ID, and actions like scroll are not sent twice.
fails: The GA4 tag loads twice (store app plus GTM, or a pasted code), so visits, events and orders can be counted twice.
validate: Browser: on the phone and desktop visit of home, collection, product and cart, count gtag/js loads and g/collect page_view hits per measurement ID per page load; flag any ID with two loads or two page_view hits for one load, and duplicate scroll or click events.
action: Keep one way of sending data to GA4 (the store app or GTM) and ask your developer to remove the other.
done_when: Our re-visit shows one GA4 load and one page_view per page for each measurement ID.
why_it_matters: Double counting makes visits look high and conversion low, so you fix the wrong things.
selected_because: Tested on real audits and failed on 3 of 5 stores; fully visible from our headless visit.

title: Popular products that people view but don't add
pass: No much-viewed product adds to cart at far below your store average.
fails: A product with many views adds to cart at under half your store average; it is named.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[pagePath,eventName] metrics=[eventCount] for view_item and add_to_cart; our headless visit opens that product.
action: Fix that product page: price, photos, Arabic title, size or option info and stock. The page review checks this exact product.
done_when: That product's add-to-cart rate reaches your store average.
why_it_matters: Your most-viewed product that doesn't sell is where your visits are lost.
selected_because: Names a specific product the owner can fix in the product editor today.

title: Landing pages with visits but no sales
pass: No high-traffic landing page converts at under a third of your store average.
fails: A top landing page converts at under a third of your store average; it is named.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[landingPage] metrics=[sessions,conversions] ordered by sessions.
action: Fix that page, or send your ads and links to a page that sells until it is fixed.
done_when: The page converts at half your store average or more, or no paid traffic lands on it.
why_it_matters: Visits that land on a page that doesn't sell are money spent with nothing back.
selected_because: Named page, clear owner action, measurable today.

title: Free-delivery threshold vs your average order
pass: A free-delivery threshold is shown on the store and sits a little above your average order value (1.1 to 1.6 times).
fails: No free-delivery threshold is shown, or it sits below or far above your average order value.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: purchaseRevenue / transactions for the average order value; the threshold is read from the live store pages and cart in our headless visit.
action: In your store's delivery settings, set free delivery a little above your average order value and show it in the cart.
done_when: The threshold is set at 1.2 to 1.5 times your average order value and shows in the cart on a phone.
why_it_matters: A threshold just above the usual order nudges shoppers to add one more item.
selected_because: GCC free-delivery lever scored high in the spec; owner sets it in the admin.

title: Paid campaign that brings visits but no sales
pass: No paid campaign with real volume converts near zero.
fails: A paid campaign brings many visits and almost no sales; it is named with its landing page.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionCampaignName,sessionDefaultChannelGroup,landingPage] metrics=[sessions,conversions].
action: Pause that campaign or point it to a page that sells.
done_when: The campaign is paused, or its conversion rate is up after the change.
why_it_matters: Ad visits that never buy cost you money every day the campaign runs.
selected_because: Direct waste the owner can stop; measurable from GA4 without ad accounts.

title: Bringing buyers back
pass: Returning visitors convert at 2 times new visitors or more, or the store already collects WhatsApp numbers or emails.
fails: Returning visitors convert at under 2 times new visitors and the store has no WhatsApp or email signup.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[newVsReturning] metrics=[sessions,conversions]; our headless visit looks for a WhatsApp or email signup.
action: Add a WhatsApp or email signup with a first-order offer, and send a message after each purchase.
done_when: The signup is live on the store and the returning-visitor share rises month on month.
why_it_matters: A past buyer is cheaper to sell to again than a new visitor.
selected_because: Retention is a top ICP1 pain; WhatsApp is their channel.

title: Tabby, Tamara or your payment page taking credit for sales
pass: No payment provider or checkout domain shows as a traffic source.
fails: tabby, tamara, a bank, a payment gateway or a checkout domain shows as a source, so orders are credited to it instead of the ad or link that brought the buyer.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionSource,sessionMedium] metrics=[sessions,conversions]; match sources against the gateway list.
action: In GA4, add those domains to the unwanted referrals list of your web data stream.
done_when: They no longer appear as traffic sources in GA4.
why_it_matters: When payment pages take the credit, you can't see which ads and links really bring sales.
selected_because: Common GCC failure (BNPL redirects) with a one-step owner fix.

title: GA4 uses your currency and time zone
pass: The GA4 property currency and time zone match the country most of your sales come from.
fails: Currency or time zone doesn't match your main market, so revenue shows in the wrong currency and daily sales don't line up with your store admin.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: get_property (currencyCode, timeZone) compared with the top country by sessions and purchases.
action: In GA4 property settings, set the currency and time zone to your store's market.
done_when: Property settings show your store's currency and time zone.
why_it_matters: Money figures in the wrong currency or day make every sales number in the report harder to trust.
selected_because: Directly decides whether the money number is in the store's currency (ICP rule).

title: Visits and sales with no known source
pass: Unassigned and (not set) are under 10% of visits, and campaign names in GA4 are clean (no broken or placeholder values).
fails: Over 10% of visits have no known source, or links carry broken or mixed-case campaign tags that GA4 can't sort.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions]; new check: run_report dimensions=[sessionSource,sessionMedium,sessionCampaignName] to flag placeholder text, encoded characters and case variants of the same source.
action: Add simple, lowercase campaign tags to every ad, Instagram bio, WhatsApp and SMS link.
done_when: Unassigned visits are under 5% in GA4 and no broken campaign names appear.
why_it_matters: If you can't see where sales come from, you can't put more into what works.
selected_because: Measurable today; merges four candidates that all measure unknown or misfiled sources.

title: Campaign credit lost on the way into your store
pass: A link with campaign tags keeps them through any redirect, and links inside the store carry no campaign tags.
fails: A redirect (http to https, www, language page) drops the campaign tags, or banners and menu links inside the store carry campaign tags that overwrite the real source.
validate: Browser: open the home page with test utm_ parameters on phone and desktop and check the page_location of the first GA4 page_view after redirects still has them. Crawl: scan internal links on home, collection, product and cart for utm_ parameters.
action: Remove campaign tags from links inside your store; ask your developer to keep the tags through redirects.
done_when: Our re-visit shows the tags kept after redirects and no internal links with campaign tags.
why_it_matters: When the tags drop, sales from your ads show up as direct visits and good campaigns look weak.
selected_because: Both checkable from our visit and crawl; they are one question: does the store keep the real source.

title: Test and preview sites sending data into your real numbers
pass: Only your real store domain(s) send visits and purchases to this GA4 property.
fails: Preview, staging, theme-editor, localhost or unknown hostnames send visits or test purchases into the live numbers.
validate: New GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[hostName] metrics=[sessions,transactions,purchaseRevenue]; flag hostnames that are not the store's domains seen in the crawl.
action: Ask your developer to stop test and preview sites from sending to this GA4 property, and to filter out unknown hostnames.
done_when: Only your store's domains appear in the hostname report.
why_it_matters: Test orders and fake hosts add sales that never happened, so your revenue looks higher than it is.
selected_because: Turns two hard-to-check candidates into one GA4 hostname query that directly protects the sales number.

title: Only real sales count as conversions
pass: purchase is a key event, no noise events (page view, scroll, session start) are, and no key event has recorded nothing in the period.
fails: purchase is not a key event, noise events are marked as key events, or a key event has no data.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: list_key_events; new check: run_report 90 days dimensions=[eventName] metrics=[eventCount] to flag key events with zero count.
action: In GA4, mark purchase as a key event and unmark page view, scroll and anything that isn't a sale or lead.
done_when: The key events list shows only real sales and leads, each with data.
why_it_matters: When page views count as conversions, your conversion rate looks good while sales stay flat.
selected_because: Tested; decides whether the conversion rate the owner reads is real.

title: What shoppers search for on your store
pass: Search is visible on phones and searches are recorded in GA4.
fails: Shoppers search but search is hidden on phones, or searches aren't recorded so nobody sees what they look for.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[searchTerm] metrics=[eventCount]; our phone visit checks the search icon in the header.
action: Show search in the phone header and make sure your top searched words, Arabic and English, return products.
done_when: Search shows in the phone header and the top 5 searched words return products.
why_it_matters: A shopper who searches knows what they want; a search with no result is a lost sale.
selected_because: Owner-fixable, gives real customer demand from their own data.

title: Sales recorded per product
pass: Purchased items carry product names, and item revenue adds up to order revenue within 5%.
fails: Item names show as (not set), or item revenue doesn't add up to order revenue, so you can't see which products sell.
validate: New GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[itemName] metrics=[itemRevenue,itemsPurchased]; share of (not set) item rows; compare total itemRevenue with purchaseRevenue for the same period.
action: Ask your developer to send each purchased product's name, ID, price and quantity with the order.
done_when: Product names show in GA4's items report and item revenue adds up to order revenue within 5%.
why_it_matters: Without product sales, you can't tell which products to push, restock or drop.
selected_because: Product-level sales are an owner decision tool; both candidates measure the same item data.

title: Customer emails and phone numbers in GA4
pass: No email addresses or phone numbers appear in page addresses sent to GA4.
fails: Emails or phone numbers appear in page paths or URL parameters sent to GA4.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[pagePath,pageLocation] scanning for @, %40, email=, phone=, mobile= and long digit strings.
action: Ask your developer to remove personal data from page addresses, and turn on email and URL redaction in the GA4 data stream.
done_when: No emails or phone numbers appear in page paths.
why_it_matters: Google can delete a property's data for this, and you would lose your sales history.
selected_because: Protects the owner's whole data history; redaction candidates are the fix for the same failure.

title: Visits from countries you don't deliver to
pass: Countries with a real share of visits also produce sales.
fails: Countries with a real share of visits and no sales; they are named.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[country] metrics=[sessions,conversions].
action: Exclude those countries from your ad targeting, or add delivery to them if you want those buyers.
done_when: Paid visits from those countries are close to zero, or they start to produce sales.
why_it_matters: Visits from places you can't deliver to never become sales.
selected_because: Simple waste check with a clear owner action; measurable today.

title: Hours and days your store sells best
pass: Conversion is about even across the day and week, or your ads and messages already follow the best times.
fails: Some hours or days convert far better than others, with enough visits to act on.
validate: Computed GA4 fact: run_report 28 days dimensions=[dayOfWeek,hour] metrics=[sessions,conversions].
action: Run more of your ads, offers and WhatsApp messages in the hours and days that sell best.
done_when: Your ad schedule and message times match the best hours and days.
why_it_matters: Putting your budget and messages where shoppers buy gets more sales from the same spend.
selected_because: Owner-actionable timing insight from their own data; beats ad-side admin points for this reader.

title: Tracking runs on every page of your store
pass: The GTM container snippet for the store's own container ID loads on the live home, collection, product and cart pages, on phone and desktop.
fails: GTM is missing from some page types (often product or cart pages, or a theme template that was swapped), or the live site loads a different or no container, so visits and sales on those pages are not recorded.
validate: Crawl the HTML source of home, one collection, one product and the cart, and check the headless phone and desktop visits for a gtm.js request with the same GTM-ID as the container read through the service account. Fail if any page type has no request or a different ID.
action: Ask your developer to add the GTM code to the shared store layout so it loads on every page, including product and cart pages.
done_when: Our re-scan finds the same GTM container loading on home, collection, product and cart pages on phone and desktop.
why_it_matters: Pages without tracking show up as visits and sales you never made, so your sales report and funnel read wrong.
selected_because: Without the container on every page no other tracking point can work; tested in audits, failed on 3 of 5 stores.

title: Each order is counted once, not again on refresh
pass: Every purchase and conversion tag fires on the dataLayer purchase event only, sends transaction_id, and has no extra trigger (no thank-you URL page view, no All Pages trigger, no trigger group missing a condition).
fails: A purchase tag fires on a thank-you page URL, so reloading or revisiting that page counts the order again; or a conversion tag is tied to a broad trigger and fires on unrelated pages.
validate: GTM read: for each purchase/conversion tag, list its firing triggers; fail if any is a page-view trigger with a thank-you/order URL filter, an All Pages trigger, or a trigger group without the purchase event condition; fail if transaction_id is not sent.
action: Have your developer fire purchase tags only on the purchase event and send the order number with it.
done_when: Every purchase tag in GTM has one trigger on the purchase event and sends transaction_id.
why_it_matters: Double-counted orders make your sales and conversion rate look higher than the money in your bank.
selected_because: An inflated order count makes every money number in the report untrustworthy for the owner.

title: Orders carry their value, currency and products
pass: Every purchase tag sends value, currency (the store's currency, from a variable) and items.
fails: Value, currency or items missing, or currency typed by hand in one tag and missing in another, so revenue shows as zero, in the wrong currency, or without products.
validate: GTM read: read the parameters of the GA4 purchase tag and any pixel purchase tags; fail if value, currency or items is missing or currency is a hard-coded different code from the store's currency.
action: Have your developer send order value, your store's currency and the products bought with every purchase tag.
done_when: All purchase tags in GTM send value, currency and items, with currency taken from one variable.
why_it_matters: Without value and currency your revenue and average order value in GA4 are wrong, so you cannot see what sales you are losing.
selected_because: Revenue is the owner's main number; missing value or currency breaks every money figure.

title: Shopify checkout and orders are tracked
pass: The store is not on Shopify, or begin_checkout and purchase come from a Shopify Customer Events pixel or the native Google and YouTube integration.
fails: A Shopify store relies on GTM tags for checkout and purchase, but GTM does not run inside Shopify checkout, so those steps are missing or partial.
validate: Platform from the crawl and headless visit; GTM read for begin_checkout and purchase tags and their triggers; headless visit for the Shopify web-pixels / Customer Events sandbox scripts. Fail on Shopify when checkout/purchase depend on GTM tags only.
action: On Shopify, have your developer send checkout and purchase from a custom pixel in Settings > Customer events, or the native Google integration.
done_when: Checkout and purchase events come from a Customer Events pixel or the native integration, not from GTM tags alone.
why_it_matters: If checkout and orders are not recorded, GA4 cannot show your real sales or where shoppers drop out of checkout.
selected_because: A common Shopify gap that removes the last and most valuable funnel steps.

title: Every buying step is tracked so you can see the leak
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Tags exist and have triggers for view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase.
fails: One or more of these steps has no tag or no trigger, so the funnel has a gap and the step losing the most sales cannot be found.
validate: GTM read: list GA4 event tags by event name and their triggers; fail if any of the four events has no active tag with a firing trigger.
action: Have your developer add the missing steps (product view, add to cart, checkout start, purchase) to GTM.
done_when: All four steps have an active tag with a trigger in GTM.
why_it_matters: You can only fix the step that loses sales if every step is counted.
selected_because: The funnel money finding depends on all four steps being tracked.

title: Add to cart is counted when shoppers really add
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Our real Add-to-Cart click on a product page produced one add_to_cart event, including from a cart drawer or quick add.
fails: Add to cart fires only on a form submit or page change, so drawer and quick adds are not counted; or it fires on the click even when nothing was added.
validate: Headless phone visit: click Add to Cart on one product, confirm the cart count changed, and check the dataLayer and network for exactly one add_to_cart hit; GTM read for the add_to_cart trigger type.
action: Have your developer trigger add to cart from your theme's own add-to-cart event, not from a click or a page change.
done_when: A test add to cart on phone produces one add_to_cart event and the cart shows the item.
why_it_matters: A wrong add-to-cart count hides whether your product pages or your cart are losing the sale.
selected_because: Directly measured on the live store; decides which page the owner fixes first.

title: Each ad pixel is installed once, not twice
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: Each ad pixel (Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, Google) loads from one source only: a store app, GTM, or code, not two or three at once.
fails: The same pixel is added by a Salla, Zid or Shopify app and again through GTM or pasted code, so page views, add to carts and purchases are sent twice.
validate: Headless visit of home, product and cart: count base-pixel loads and event hits per pixel ID in the network log; compare with pixel tags in the GTM read. Fail if one pixel ID loads from more than one source or sends duplicate events for one action.
action: Pick one way to install each pixel (the store's app or GTM) and remove the other; you can switch off the app integration yourself, the GTM tag needs your developer.
done_when: Our re-scan sees each pixel ID load once and send one event per action.
why_it_matters: Double-sent sales make your ads look better than they are, so you may spend more on ads that do not sell.
selected_because: Tested in audits, failed on 2 of 3 stores; the owner can fix part of it in the admin.

title: Consent settings do not hide your Gulf visitors
pass: Consent defaults are set per region, or the consent banner applies only where required, so visits from GCC markets are recorded normally.
fails: All tags are denied by default for every region, including markets with no such requirement, so many visits and sales are never recorded.
validate: GTM read: consent default tag parameters (region list, ad_storage, analytics_storage); headless visit without clicking the banner: decode the gcs/gcd parameter on GA4 hits to see whether storage is denied.
action: Have your developer set consent defaults per region so visitors in your markets are counted.
done_when: Consent default lists the regions that need it, and our visit from a GCC location sends GA4 hits with storage granted.
why_it_matters: Visits and orders blocked by consent disappear from your reports, so your sales look lower than they are.
selected_because: An over-strict banner removes real GCC sales from the owner's numbers.

title: WhatsApp and call clicks are counted
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Clicks on WhatsApp and phone links fire an event, or the store has no such links.
fails: The store shows a WhatsApp or call button but no tag records the click, so orders that start in WhatsApp are invisible.
validate: Headless visit lists wa.me, api.whatsapp.com and tel: links; GTM read for link-click triggers on those URLs and the event they send. Fail if links exist and no tag tracks them.
action: Have your developer track WhatsApp and call button clicks as an event in GTM.
done_when: A click on the WhatsApp button sends an event, visible in our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Shoppers who order through WhatsApp look like lost visitors, so you cannot see which pages and ads bring them.
selected_because: WhatsApp is a main sales channel for GCC stores and is usually untracked.

title: Every ad platform you pay for gets your sales
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: Every paid social channel that brings traffic (Meta, Snapchat, TikTok) has its pixel with add-to-cart and purchase events.
fails: GA4 shows paid traffic from Snapchat, TikTok or Meta, but that platform's pixel or its add-to-cart and purchase events are missing.
validate: GA4 report: paid channels by source; GTM read and headless visit: pixel tags and events present per platform. Fail if a paying channel has no pixel or no purchase event.
action: Have your developer add the missing platform's pixel with add-to-cart and purchase events.
done_when: Each platform sending paid visits has a pixel with add-to-cart and purchase in GTM.
why_it_matters: An ad platform that never sees your sales cannot find more buyers like them.
selected_because: Ties tracking to ad money the owner already spends.

title: Tracking tags do not slow your store on phones
group_en: Tags that fit your store and keep it fast
group_ar: أكواد التتبع تناسب متجرك وما تبطّئه
pass: Only core tags fire on All Pages; heavy third-party tags load only on the pages that need them, and GTM does not delay the main content on phone.
