fails: Many heavy tags or Custom HTML tags fire on every page, adding scripts that slow phone loading and move the layout.
validate: GTM read: tags on the All Pages trigger and the scripts they load; headless phone visit: count and weight of scripts loaded by GTM and their timing against first content paint and layout shift.
action: Have your developer limit heavy tags to the pages that need them and remove tags no one uses.
done_when: Only core tags fire on All Pages and our phone visit loads fewer GTM scripts than before.
why_it_matters: A slower store on phones means more shoppers leave before they see your products.
selected_because: Links tracking setup to a sales effect the owner understands: phone speed.

title: Visits are counted once
pass: One Google tag per GA4 measurement ID and no extra page_view tag on top of the automatic one.
fails: Two Google tags for the same ID, or a manual page_view tag, so each visit is counted twice and the conversion rate looks lower than it is.
validate: GTM read: count Google tag / GA4 config tags per measurement ID and GA4 event tags named page_view; headless visit: count page_view hits per page load.
action: Have your developer delete the duplicate Google tag or the extra page view tag.
done_when: Our visit sees one page_view per page load.
why_it_matters: Double-counted visits make your conversion rate look worse and hide which pages really sell.
selected_because: Changes the conversion rate the owner sees.

title: Your data goes to your own GA4 only
pass: Every GA4 tag uses one constant variable holding the store's own measurement ID.
fails: Old or hard-coded IDs send visits and sales to another GA4 property, such as one from a past agency.
validate: GTM read: collect every G- ID in tags and variables; headless visit: list G- IDs in GA4 hits. Fail if any ID is not the store's connected property.
action: Have your developer keep one GA4 ID in one variable and remove the others.
done_when: Only your own GA4 ID appears in GTM and in our visit.
why_it_matters: Sales sent to another property are missing from your reports, and someone else can see your sales.
selected_because: Split data hides part of the owner's sales.

title: Product names and prices reach your reports
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Ecommerce tags send items with item_id, item_name, price and quantity, read from the right dataLayer fields.
fails: Items are missing or lack id, price or quantity, often because a variable reads the wrong dataLayer path and returns empty.
validate: GTM read: ecommerce tags' items setting and dataLayer variable paths; headless visit: check view_item and add_to_cart hits for item_id, item_name, price and quantity.
action: Have your developer send product id, name, price and quantity with every shopping event.
done_when: Our visit's view_item and add_to_cart hits carry all four product fields.
why_it_matters: Without product data you cannot see which products sell and which get views but no sales.
selected_because: Product reports show the owner which products to fix or push.

title: Ad pixel loads before its events
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: Each pixel's base tag loads before its event tags (by tag sequencing or priority), so add-to-cart and purchase events are received.
fails: Event tags fire before the base pixel is ready, so some add-to-cart or purchase events are lost.
validate: GTM read: setup-tag sequencing and firing priority on pixel event tags; headless visit: order of base-pixel load and event hits in the network log.
action: Have your developer set each pixel's base tag to load before its event tags.
done_when: Every pixel event tag has the base tag as its setup tag, and our visit sees the base load first.
why_it_matters: Lost events mean your ad platforms see fewer sales than you made.
selected_because: Tested in audits, failed on 2 of 3 stores; causes sales to go missing in ad platforms.

title: Meta does not count the same sale twice
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: The Meta Purchase event fires with an event_id that can match a server event, or Meta is not used.
fails: The Meta pixel is present without a Purchase event, or without an event_id, so Meta cannot match browser and server sales.
validate: GTM read: Meta pixel tags (Custom HTML or template) and their event name and eventID parameters; headless visit: event_id present on Meta hits we can trigger (view content, add to cart).
action: Have your developer send Purchase to Meta with an order-based event_id, and use the same id in the Conversions API if you use it.
done_when: The Meta Purchase tag in GTM sends an event_id.
why_it_matters: Without a matching id Meta can count one sale twice or miss it, so you cannot trust Meta's sales number.
selected_because: Meta is the main paid channel for GCC stores.

title: Customer details are not sent to ad platforms
pass: No raw email, phone or name in tag parameters or page URLs; any customer data a platform asks for is hashed and sent only with consent.
fails: Email or phone is sent as plain text in a tag, or forms put customer details into the page URL that GA4 then stores.
validate: GTM read: scan tag parameters and dataLayer variables for email or phone fields and hashing settings; headless visit: scan network hits and URLs on the pages we visit for email or phone patterns.
action: Have your developer remove plain customer details from tags and URLs, or hash them where the platform requires it.
done_when: No plain email or phone appears in GTM tags or in our visit's network hits.
why_it_matters: Sending customer details in plain text puts your customers' trust and your accounts at risk.
selected_because: A real risk the owner is responsible for, kept as one merged privacy point.

title: Google Ads sees your sales
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: When Google Ads traffic exists, a Google Ads conversion tag and the Conversion Linker are present (or GA4 conversions are imported), with enhanced conversions on.
fails: GA4 shows Google Ads traffic but there is no conversion tag or linker, or enhanced conversions are off.
validate: GA4 report: google / cpc sessions; GTM read: awct and Conversion Linker tags and the enhanced conversions setting on the tag.
action: Have your developer add the Google Ads purchase tag and the Conversion Linker, with enhanced conversions.
done_when: GTM has a Google Ads purchase tag and Conversion Linker, both with active triggers.
why_it_matters: Google Ads can only find more buyers if it sees which clicks became sales.
selected_because: Relevant when the owner pays for Google Ads, shown only then.

title: Sales are credited to the ad that brought them
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: Ad click IDs (gclid, fbclid, ttclid, ScCid) are stored when a shopper lands from an ad.
fails: Paid visitors arrive with click IDs and nothing stores them, so the sale cannot be tied back to the ad.
validate: Headless visit to a product page with test gclid, fbclid and ttclid parameters added to the URL; check first-party cookies (_gcl_aw, _fbc, _ttp or similar) after load; GTM read for the Conversion Linker and URL-parameter variables.
action: Have your developer add the Conversion Linker and store ad click IDs in first-party cookies.
done_when: Our test visit with click IDs leaves matching first-party cookies.
why_it_matters: When the click is not stored, sales show up as unknown, and you cannot tell which ads sell.
selected_because: Lets the owner see which ads bring sales.

title: No unknown scripts running on your store
pass: Every Custom HTML tag has a known purpose and owner, and official tag templates are used where they exist.
fails: Custom HTML tags load scripts from unknown vendors, or hand-pasted pixel code is used where an official template exists and breaks without notice.
validate: GTM read: list Custom HTML tags, the domains their scripts load, and whether an official template exists for that vendor; headless visit: domains loaded by GTM.
action: Have your developer remove scripts no one recognises and switch hand-pasted pixels to official templates.
done_when: Every Custom HTML tag in GTM has a named purpose, and known pixels use official templates.
why_it_matters: Unknown scripts can break your pages or collect your customers' data without you knowing.
selected_because: A risk the owner can ask about and verify.

title: Old agency and campaign tags removed
group_en: Tags that fit your store and keep it fast
group_ar: أكواد التتبع تناسب متجرك وما تبطّئه
pass: No paused tags, tags with no trigger, or pixels from past vendors and ended campaigns.
fails: Tags from a past agency or old campaigns still load on every visit, slowing pages and sending your data to vendors you no longer use.
validate: GTM read: paused flag, tags without firing triggers, vendor names and IDs not matching current platforms; headless visit: requests to those vendors.
action: Have your developer delete dead and past-vendor tags.
done_when: GTM has no paused, trigger-less or past-vendor tags.
why_it_matters: Old tags slow your store and keep sending your data to people you stopped working with.
selected_because: Easy cleanup with a speed and data-risk effect the owner understands.

title: Consent banner works before and after the choice
pass: Where a consent banner is used, the consent default fires on Consent Initialization before any tag, and marketing tags require ad_storage consent.
fails: The consent default is missing or loads late, or pixels fire with no consent check, so the banner has no real effect.
validate: GTM read: consent tag trigger (Consent Initialization - All Pages) and each marketing tag's consent settings; headless visit: whether pixel hits are sent before any banner choice.
action: Have your developer load consent defaults first and link marketing tags to consent.
done_when: Consent default runs on Consent Initialization and each marketing tag lists its consent requirement.
why_it_matters: A banner that does not work exposes you to complaints from customers in regions that require consent.
selected_because: Kept as one low point; matters mainly for stores selling outside the GCC.

title: Your team's visits are kept out of sales numbers
group_en: Tags that fit your store and keep it fast
group_ar: أكواد التتبع تناسب متجرك وما تبطّئه
pass: A traffic_type parameter, IP rule or logged-in-staff exception marks your team's own visits.
fails: Nothing marks the team's visits, so your own browsing and test orders mix with real customers.
validate: GTM read: traffic_type parameter on the Google tag, or a blocking exception for staff or admin sessions.
action: Have your developer mark your team's visits so GA4 can leave them out.
done_when: The Google tag sends traffic_type for team visits, or staff sessions are blocked.
why_it_matters: Your own visits make conversion rate and product views look different from what customers do.
selected_because: Small, clean fix that makes the owner's numbers truer.

title: See what shoppers search for
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Searches on the store record a search or view_search_results event with the search term.
fails: The store has a search box and nothing records the term, so you cannot see what shoppers look for and do not find.
validate: Headless visit: run one search and check for a search / view_search_results hit with the term; GTM read for a search tag or the search URL parameter setting.
action: Have your developer record store searches with the search term.
done_when: A test search sends an event with the term.
why_it_matters: Search terms show which products shoppers want that you do not show or stock.
selected_because: Gives the owner product and wording ideas from real demand.

title: Session recordings installed to check your fixes
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Microsoft Clarity or Hotjar is installed and its script actually loads on the live store.
fails: No recording tool, or a tag set up in GTM that never loads on the live site.
validate: GTM read for Clarity or Hotjar tags; crawl and headless visit for their script requests on live pages. We only check that it loads; we do not read its data.
action: Install Microsoft Clarity (free) through GTM or your store's app so you can watch how shoppers use the pages you fix.
done_when: Our re-scan sees the recording script load on home and product pages.
why_it_matters: Recordings let you see whether a fix helped shoppers, not just guess.
selected_because: Tested in audits, failed on 3 of 4 stores; helps the owner confirm fixes.

title: Add to cart actually adds the product
pass: On a phone, our tap on Add to cart put the product in the cart and the cart count went up.
fails: The tap does nothing, shows an error, or the cart stays empty, so a customer who wants to buy cannot.
validate: Headless phone visit of one product page: tap Add to cart, then read the cart count, the cart drawer or cart page, and the network response of the add request. Fail when the item is not in the cart afterwards.
action: Ask your developer to fix the Add to cart button or the theme script behind it, then test it yourself on your phone.
done_when: A tap on Add to cart on a phone adds the product and the cart count updates, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: If the button does not add the product, every customer who decided to buy leaves without an order.
selected_because: A broken Add to cart stops all sales on that page; highest direct sales effect in this section.

title: The cart opens without errors
pass: The cart page loads fully on phone and desktop with no script errors and no failed loads.
fails: Script errors, repeating errors or a failed load on the cart, so totals, buttons or the checkout button may not work.
validate: Headless phone and desktop visit of the cart after our add to cart: collect console errors, uncaught exceptions and failed requests (status 400 or more) on the cart. Fail on any error that repeats or any failed load of the cart's own scripts. Checkout itself is not visited.
action: Send the error list from this report to your developer and ask them to clear every error on the cart page.
done_when: Zero console errors and zero failed loads when the cart opens, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Customers who reach the cart already chose to buy; an error here loses them at the last step we can see.
selected_because: Cart errors block people who already want to buy; merged with the console-error check (same measurement).

title: Product page shows fast on phones
pass: On a phone, the main product image or title shows in under 2.5 seconds (LCP).
fails: The main content of the product page takes longer than 2.5 seconds to show on a phone, so some visitors leave before they see the product.
validate: Headless phone visit of the product page with a throttled mobile profile: read LCP and the element that was the LCP. Fail when LCP is over 2.5 seconds. Repeat on home and collection for context.
action: Make the main product photo smaller in file size and ask your developer to load it first, before apps and banners.
done_when: LCP on the product page is under 2.5 seconds on a phone, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: A product page that shows late loses visitors before they see the price or the Add to cart button.
selected_because: Slow mobile product pages failed in 3 of 4 tested stores and most GCC traffic is on phones.

title: WhatsApp and call buttons reach you
pass: Every WhatsApp (wa.me or api.whatsapp.com) and phone (tel:) link uses a full international number, or the store has none.
fails: A WhatsApp or call link has a missing, local-format or malformed number, so a customer who wants to ask before buying cannot reach you.
validate: Headless visit of home, collection, product and cart: collect every wa.me, api.whatsapp.com and tel: link and check each number is present and in full international format with the country code.
action: Fix the number in your WhatsApp button or app settings so it starts with your country code (for Saudi numbers, 966) with no leading zero.
done_when: Every WhatsApp and call link on the store opens a chat or call to your number, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Many GCC customers ask on WhatsApp before they order; a broken link sends those orders away.
selected_because: WhatsApp is the GCC customer's main question channel; owner can fix it in minutes.

title: Google can show your products and collections
pass: Product and collection pages are allowed in robots.txt and carry no noindex or nofollow tag.
fails: A noindex tag, an X-Robots-Tag header or a robots.txt rule blocks product or collection pages, so they cannot appear in Google.
validate: Public crawl: fetch robots.txt and the sitemap, then the HTML and headers of the visited product and collection pages plus a sample of sitemap URLs. Fail on any noindex/nofollow meta, X-Robots-Tag, or robots.txt Disallow that covers product or collection URLs.
action: Turn off any setting or app that hides your products from search engines, or ask your developer to remove the noindex tag.
done_when: Product and collection pages show no noindex and are not blocked in robots.txt, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Blocked pages get no free visits from Google, so you pay for every visitor through ads.
selected_because: A block removes all free search traffic to the pages that sell; a sales effect, not SEO polish.

title: Your sales value is recorded with every shopping step
pass: view_item and add_to_cart carry value, currency and an items list with item_id and item_name (GA4 field names) in the dataLayer and the GA4 hit.
fails: Value, currency or items are missing, use old field names, or the dataLayer push is malformed, so GA4 shows blank or wrong product and sales figures.
validate: Headless visit: read the dataLayer pushes and GA4 collect hits for view_item on the product page and add_to_cart after our click. Fail when value, currency or items[] is missing, items use legacy names (id, name instead of item_id, item_name), or the push is not a valid ecommerce object.
action: Ask your developer to send value, currency and the product list with every shopping event, using the GA4 field names.
done_when: Our re-scan sees value, currency, item_id and item_name on view_item and add_to_cart.
why_it_matters: Without these fields your reports cannot show which products sell or what each step is worth in money.
selected_because: Missing value or items blanks the sales numbers the owner reads; dataLayer format failed in 3 of 5 tested stores.

title: Each order is counted once in GA4
pass: In GA4, every purchase has its own transaction ID and no ID appears on more than one purchase.
fails: The same transaction ID is recorded on two or more purchases, or purchases arrive with an empty transaction ID, so GA4 sales read higher than real orders.
validate: GA4 Data API, last 28 days: dimension transactionId, metrics ecommercePurchases and purchaseRevenue. Fail when any transactionId has more than one purchase, or when purchases have an empty or (not set) transactionId. Report the count and the revenue on duplicated IDs.
action: Ask your developer to send the store's order number as the transaction ID and to stop the purchase event firing again when the thank-you page is reopened.
done_when: No transaction ID has more than one purchase in GA4 over 14 days.
why_it_matters: Double-counted orders make your GA4 sales look better than your real sales, so you decide on the wrong numbers.
selected_because: Duplicate orders change the sales figure the owner sees; readable from GA4 without reaching checkout.

title: Recorded price and currency match the price on the page
pass: The value sent with view_item and add_to_cart equals the price shown on the product page (times quantity), and currency is the store's three-letter code in capitals (for example SAR).
fails: Currency is a symbol, lowercase, a different code from the store's, or the value is off by a factor (for example 1000x from a comma or dot read the wrong way).
validate: Headless visit: read the displayed price on the product page and the value and currency in the view_item and add_to_cart dataLayer pushes and GA4 hits. Fail when currency is not an uppercase ISO 4217 code matching the store's currency, or the value differs from the displayed price beyond rounding.
action: Ask your developer to send the price as a plain number and the currency as the three-letter code your store charges in.
done_when: Our re-scan sees the same price and the correct currency code in the event as on the page.
why_it_matters: A wrong currency or price makes every sales figure in your reports wrong, even when orders are fine.
selected_because: Wrong currency or price corrupts all revenue reporting the owner reads; checkable against the page price.

title: Every shopping step is recorded
pass: Our visit produced view_item_list on the collection, view_item on the product and add_to_cart after our click, with standard GA4 event names.
fails: One of these steps sends no event, or sends it under a custom name, so GA4 cannot show where customers drop off.
validate: Headless visit of collection, product and our add to cart: read dataLayer pushes and GA4 collect hits. Fail when view_item_list, view_item or add_to_cart is missing or only sent under a non-standard name.
action: Ask your developer to send the standard GA4 events on the collection page, the product page and Add to cart.
done_when: Our re-scan sees view_item_list, view_item and add_to_cart with these exact names.
why_it_matters: If a step is not recorded, the report cannot tell you which step is losing sales.
selected_because: Missing steps hide where sales are lost; standard names failed in 3 of 5 tested stores.

title: Visits and events are not counted twice
pass: One page_view per page load and one hit per event, with no blocked tracking requests.
fails: Two tracking setups (for example a store app plus a separate tag) send page_view or add_to_cart twice, or requests are blocked, so visit and conversion numbers are wrong.
validate: Headless visit: count GA4 collect hits per page load and per event, grouped by measurement ID. Fail on more than one page_view per load, a repeated event from one action, or tracking requests blocked by the site's own security policy.
action: Ask your developer to keep one tracking setup and remove the duplicate.
done_when: One page_view per page and one add_to_cart per click, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Double counting makes your conversion rate look lower or higher than it is, so you fix the wrong thing.
selected_because: Duplicates distort the conversion rate the owner sees; one merged network check.

title: Tracking loads on every page type
pass: The GA4 tag (directly or through GTM) loads on home, collection, product and cart.
fails: The tag is missing on one page type, so visits and sales on that page are not counted.
validate: Headless visit of home, collection, product and cart: confirm a GA4 or GTM script loads and at least one GA4 collect hit is sent on each.
action: Ask your developer to add the tracking tag to the page type where it is missing.
done_when: Our re-scan sees GA4 hits on home, collection, product and cart.
why_it_matters: A page with no tracking is a blind spot: its visitors and sales disappear from your numbers.
selected_because: A missing tag removes a page from every sales figure in the report.

title: No sold-out products where shoppers look first
pass: No sold-out product appears in the home banner or the first row of the home page or collection.
fails: A sold-out product is featured in the banner or first row, so the first product a customer opens cannot be bought.
validate: Headless visit of home and the collection: read the products in the hero and first row and their stock state from the page and product schema. Fail when any is sold out.
action: Swap sold-out products out of your home banner and first row, or turn on the setting that moves sold-out products to the end.
done_when: No sold-out product in the banner or first row, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: The products in the first row get the most taps; if they are sold out, those taps cannot become orders.
selected_because: Owner fixes it in the admin today; wastes the most-viewed spots on the store.

title: No broken images or files on the pages that sell
pass: No request returns 404 or 500 on home, collection, product or cart.
fails: Product images, scripts or styles fail to load, so pages look broken or features stop working.
validate: Headless visit of home, collection, product and cart: list network requests with status 400 or more and the page each is on.
action: Re-upload the missing images and ask your developer to fix or remove the broken files.
done_when: Zero failed requests on home, collection, product and cart, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: A missing product photo or a broken script makes the store look untrustworthy and can stop buttons working.
selected_because: Broken files hurt trust and function on the money pages; clear fix list.

title: Your ad platforms can see who buys
pass: A pixel loads and fires for each ad platform the store uses (Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, Google Ads).
fails: No pixel, or a pixel that loads but sends no events, for a platform the store advertises on.
validate: Headless visit: detect Meta, Snapchat, TikTok and Google Ads tags in the HTML and network, and check each sends PageView/ViewContent and AddToCart hits during our visit.
action: Connect the pixel for each platform you advertise on, through your store's sales-channel or app settings, or ask whoever runs your ads.
done_when: Our re-scan sees each platform's pixel fire on page view and add to cart.
why_it_matters: Without a working pixel, your ads cannot learn which visitors buy, so you pay for visitors who are less likely to order.
selected_because: Owners pay for ads; a missing pixel wastes that budget and is a quick connect in most store admins.

title: Taps respond without delay
pass: No script task longer than 200 ms while the product page loads on a phone.
fails: Long script tasks make taps on Add to cart, size or colour lag, so shoppers tap again or give up.
validate: Headless phone visit of the product page: record main-thread long tasks during load and report the longest and the scripts behind them.
action: Ask your developer to delay or remove the scripts behind the long tasks listed in this report.
done_when: No task over 200 ms on the product page, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: A button that does not react right away makes customers think the store is broken.
selected_because: Lagging taps hit the Add to cart moment on phones.

title: Product photos are not heavier than needed
pass: Images are served near the size shown, in WebP or AVIF, and images below the first screen load later.
fails: Photos are far larger than shown, in old formats, or images lower on the page load before the main photo.
validate: Headless phone visit of home, collection and product: compare each image's file size and pixel size with its displayed size, check format and loading order.
action: Resize and compress your largest photos before uploading them again; this report lists them.
done_when: No listed image is more than twice its shown size, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Heavy photos are the most common reason a store page shows slowly on a phone.
selected_because: A speed fix the owner can do without a developer.

title: Apps do not slow the store down
pass: Chat, review, popup and other app scripts load light or after the page shows.
fails: App scripts make up most of the page weight or load before the product shows.
validate: Headless phone visit: group network bytes and script time by third-party domain and name the app behind each; report the share of load each takes.
action: Remove apps you do not use and switch the heavy ones to load after the page.
done_when: No single app is the largest part of page weight on the product page, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Each app adds waiting time before customers see your product.
selected_because: Owner controls which apps are installed; direct speed effect.

title: The page does not jump while loading
pass: CLS under 0.1 on home, collection and product on a phone.
fails: Banners, images or app widgets push content down as they load, so shoppers tap the wrong thing.
validate: Headless phone visit: read CLS and the elements that moved on home, collection and product.
action: Ask your developer to reserve space for images, banners and app widgets so nothing moves after the page shows.
done_when: CLS under 0.1 on all three pages, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: When the page jumps, customers tap the wrong button and lose trust.
selected_because: Layout jumps cause mis-taps on phones; measurable on every page.

title: Product names show in full on collection pages
pass: Every product card on the collection page shows a readable product name on phone and desktop.
fails: Cards show no name, or names cut off so shoppers cannot tell products apart.
validate: Headless phone and desktop visit of the collection: for each product card, read the visible name text and check it is present and not truncated to the point of losing the product type.
action: Shorten long product titles so the key words come first, or change the theme setting that hides names.
done_when: Every product card shows a readable name, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Shoppers open the products they can recognise; unclear names mean fewer product views and fewer sales.
selected_because: Owner fixes titles in the admin; affects every collection visit.

title: The menu leads to all your categories
pass: Every collection that has products can be reached from the main menu or its sub-menus.
fails: Collections with products are missing from the menu, so shoppers cannot find those products.
validate: Public crawl plus headless visit: list collection URLs from the sitemap and the links in the header and mobile menu. List collections with products that the menu does not link to.
action: Add the missing categories to your store menu.
done_when: Every collection with products is linked from the menu, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Products shoppers cannot find through the menu are products they do not buy.
selected_because: Hidden categories cut product discovery; failed in 3 of 5 tested stores; owner edits the menu.

title: No slow or blocking code before the page shows
pass: No render-blocking scripts or styles in the head, no request over 3 seconds holding up content, and first-load code under about 1 MB.
fails: Blocking files in the head, requests that hang over 3 seconds, or more code than needed on first load delay the first view.
validate: Headless phone visit of home, collection and product: list render-blocking resources, requests longer than 3 seconds that delay visible content, and total JS plus CSS bytes on first load.
action: Send this list to your developer and ask them to delay or remove the files named.
done_when: No blocking files, no request over 3 seconds and first-load code under about 1 MB, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Code that loads before the product makes every page slower for every customer.
selected_because: Developer-only speed causes merged into one point so the owner gets one hand-over list.

title: No leftover code from apps you removed
pass: Every app script that loads belongs to an app with a visible feature on the store.
fails: Scripts still load from app domains with no visible feature, or fail to load, after the app was removed.
validate: Headless visit: list third-party script domains, match them to known apps, and flag those with no matching widget on the page or that return errors.
action: Check the listed apps; reinstall and properly uninstall them, or ask your developer to remove their leftover code from the theme.
done_when: No scripts from removed apps load, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Leftover code slows the store and can break other features, with nothing gained.
selected_because: Easy speed win the owner can start without code.

title: Google sees the right price and stock
pass: Product pages carry Product and Offer data with price and availability, and both match what the page shows.
fails: Price or stock is missing from the product data, or differs from the page, so Google can drop the product from free Shopping listings.
validate: Public crawl of the visited product page and sitemap samples: read JSON-LD Product/Offer price, currency and availability and compare them with the displayed price and stock.
action: Ask your developer to make the product data on each page show the same price and stock as the page.
done_when: Product data has price and availability that match the page, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Correct price and stock keep your products eligible for free Google Shopping listings.
selected_because: Kept only for its Google Shopping sales effect; presence and match merged into one point.

title: Shared links show a picture in WhatsApp and Instagram
pass: Home and product pages have og:title, og:image and og:description.
fails: These tags are missing, so links shared in WhatsApp or Instagram show no picture or title.
validate: Public crawl of home and product HTML: check og:title, og:image and og:description exist and the og:image URL loads.
action: Add a share image and description for your home page and products, or ask your developer to turn them on in the theme.
done_when: Home and product pages have all three tags and the image loads, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Customers share products on WhatsApp; a link with a photo gets more people to open it.
selected_because: WhatsApp sharing is a real GCC sales channel; low because it is a tag-only fix.

title: Customer emails and phone numbers stay out of page links
pass: No email address or phone number appears in page URLs or in URLs sent to tracking tools.
fails: Forms such as newsletter or contact put the customer's email or phone in the URL, which then goes to analytics and ad tools.
validate: Headless visit and crawl: inspect page URLs, form actions and tracking hit URLs (dl/dlocation parameters) for email or phone patterns.
action: Ask your developer to send form details in the request body, not in the page link.
done_when: No email or phone in any URL or tracking hit, on our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Customer details leaking to other tools is a privacy risk for your store and your customers' trust.
selected_because: The one measurable security point in the pool with a real customer-trust risk.
